title: Weeping and joy: the not-understanding that reaches the Essence
overview:
The chapter opens with the saying "weeping is lodged in my heart on one side, and joy on the other": the soul becomes a ready vessel for G-dliness only when both come together. Then the question: joy is born of comprehension, in *bina*, yet comprehension never catches Him; *chachma*, which is *ayin*, should have the joy, but its *bittul* is the opposite of joy.

The answer is that everything has its opposite, one power in two equal lines. The power of *bina* is the power of not understanding, and the Essence, beyond understanding, is what it is really after. So the weeping comes in three levels: over the explanation not yet understood, over the *hafla'a* of *chachma*, and over the Essence that can never fit in the mind. That felt emptiness is the vessel. The comprehension is of a *tzimtzum*, but the joy reaches the Essence: now through the weeping of exile, in the future as laughter. The tears of *tikkun chatzos* prepare the way; in our days the Rebbe goes straight to the joy, but *Chassidus* that does not make a man more observant is not *Chassidus*. And this explanation, Rabbi Markel says, is the *tevuna* of the Essence.

sections.title: Weeping on one side and joy on the other: the preparation of the soul
sections.summary: Before the soul can take in the knowledge of G-dliness it has to be made a ready vessel, and that is done only by weeping and joy together, two opposites from one contemplation. One without the other, or both only on the surface, is a sure sign that nothing went in.

phrases.he: (ו) והנה ידוע המאמר דבכיה תקיעא בלבאי
phrases.en: (6) Now, there is the known saying, "Weeping is lodged in my heart

phrases.he: מסטרא דא
phrases.en: from one side,

phrases.he: וחדווה מסטרא דא כו'
phrases.en: and joy from the other side."

blocks.text: Chapter 6 is really, in a way, a continuation of chapter 5. It is not about the matters of *chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding) as such, but within each one of them there is *bechiya* (weeping) and *chedva* (joy). It opens with the saying: **"Weeping is lodged in my heart** from one side, and joy from the other side." From one side is crying, from one side is happiness.

phrases.he: להיות שצריך להקדים בחינת הכנה בנפש
phrases.en: For one must first make a *hachana* (preparation) in the soul

phrases.he: לכללות הידיעה האלהי״ת בהשתלשלות דאור אין סוף
phrases.en: for the general knowledge of G-dliness, as the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) comes down

phrases.he: באבי''ע עד שתהא הנפש בחינת כלי מוכן לזה
phrases.en: through *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, until the soul is a *kli* (vessel) ready for it.

blocks.text: To take in the knowledge of G-dliness as it spreads down through the worlds, there has to be this *hachana*, **until the soul is a *kli* (vessel) ready for it**. Which means that if you do not have this *hachana*, you are not a *kli muchan*, a ready vessel.

And by the way, in our days, according to what the Rebbe says, we can really do this *lechatchila ariber* (going over the top from the start). When you start studying, the *hachana* will come on its own. That is so in general, and even in the matter of *avodas hamochin* (the service of the mind).

phrases.he: וזה אינו אלא על ידי אמצעות ב' דברים הללו דבכיה וחדווה
phrases.en: And this is only by means of these two things, weeping and joy.

phrases.he: גם שהן ב' הפכים
phrases.en: Though they are two opposites,

phrases.he: הרי באים כאחד ממש מהתבוננות אחת דווקא
phrases.en: they come together, *mamash* (actually), from one *hisbonenus* (contemplation) precisely.

phrases.he: ובזה נעשה דווקא בחינת הכנה רבה בנפש
phrases.en: And precisely by this a great preparation is made in the soul,

phrases.he: לקבוע בעצמיות שלה מכל השגות פרטיות דאור אין סוף באבי''ע
phrases.en: to fix in its very self all the particular comprehensions of the *Or Ein Sof* in *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*.

blocks.text: The *hachana* comes only through **these two things, weeping and joy**. They are two opposites, the same as before, where the *simcha* (joy) and the *bittul* (self-nullification) were two opposites. But they have to come simultaneously: in each *hisbonenus* they should come together at once. That is what makes **a great preparation** in the soul.

phrases.he: ואם יחסר אחד מאלה
phrases.en: And if one of these is missing,

phrases.he: דהיינו זה בלא זה או גם שנדמה לו
phrases.en: that is, this without that, or even if it seems to him

phrases.he: שיש בלבו משתיהם
phrases.en: that he has both in his heart,

phrases.he: אבל אינם לאמיתתם ולעומקם בנפש כלל,
phrases.en: but they are not in the soul in their truth and their depth at all,

phrases.he: רק דרך מעביר חיצוני בעלמא,
phrases.en: only in a merely external, passing way,

phrases.he: הרי זה סימן גמור שלא נקבע בנפשו כלום,
phrases.en: this is a sure sign that nothing at all has been fixed in his soul,

phrases.he: רק מרחוק מאד כו'
phrases.en: only from very far away.

phrases.he: ובמעט דבר המנגד
phrases.en: And with a little opposing thing,

phrases.he: כמו בטרדא גדולה
phrases.en: like a great preoccupation,

phrases.he: או בהרגשת עצמו ליש ביותר כו'
phrases.en: or by feeling himself very much a *yesh* (a something),

phrases.he: ינתק מלבו לגמרי כו'.
phrases.en: it will be torn from his heart completely.

blocks.text: If one is missing, if he has weeping without joy or joy without weeping, or if he only imagines that he has both, but they are not a deep thing, only something external that passes over him, **this is a sure sign that nothing at all has been fixed in his soul**. Nothing went in: the *Chassidus* did not go into him. He has it only in a very far away way.

**And with a little opposing thing**, like a lot of business to take care of, whether with his business or with whatever, or by feeling himself a real something, a *yesh*, the whole thing **will be torn from his heart completely**.

sections.title: The question: joy is in bina, and comprehension does not reach Him
sections.summary: Delight is in *chachma* and joy in *bina*, born of comprehension; yet the main joy is in G-dliness itself, and comprehension never catches Him. So the joy should be in *chachma*, which is *ayin*; but *chachma* is *bittul*, the opposite of joy.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים הנה ידוע דענג ושמחה הוא בחכמה ובינה,
phrases.en: The explanation: it is known that delight and joy are in *chachma* and *bina*:

phrases.he: הענג בחכמה ושמחה בבינה
phrases.en: the delight in *chachma*, and the joy in *bina*

phrases.he: (וזהו ההפרש בין שבת ליום טוב כידוע)
phrases.en: (and this is the difference between *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, as is known),

phrases.he: כי ההשגה בשכל מוליד השמחה
phrases.en: for comprehension in the intellect gives birth to joy,

phrases.he: שהוא שמחת הנפש
phrases.en: which is the joy of the soul,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אם הבנים שמחה
phrases.en: as it is written, "the mother of the children is joyful."

blocks.text: The explanation begins with what is known: **the delight in *chachma*, and the joy in *bina***. That is **the difference between *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov***: of *Shabbos* it says "delight", *oneg Shabbos*, and of *Yom Tov* it says "you shall rejoice in your festival". **For comprehension in the intellect gives birth to joy**, as said before: **"the mother of the children is joyful."**

phrases.he: וידוע שעיקר השמחה דווקא באלהו״ת הוא,
phrases.en: And it is known that the main joy is precisely in G-dliness,

phrases.he: וכמו וישמחו בך דוקא
phrases.en: as in "they will rejoice in You," precisely.

blocks.text: **the main joy is precisely in G-dliness**, not in the explanation. If the joy is in the explanation, that is not the real joy: **"they will rejoice in You," precisely**. Which is very strange, by the way. How is that possible? The joy of *bina* is into the *musag*, the thing grasped. The whole thing of *bina* is that it does not get to the *etzem hadavar* (the thing itself); it stops at the explanation. But it makes no difference.

blocks.title: The Steelers won
blocks.text: The joy is from the thing itself. Even when you hear about something, when you hear that something happened that makes you happy, it is not the explanation that makes you happy; it is the thing itself. Say you hear that the Steelers won. The guy tells you: then he ran, and he went to the 10th, and he went to the 5th, and then it was a thing, and it was... You hear it on the radio, from far away. But what you are happy about is not that you are hearing the explanation. It is that the guy made the goal. So the same thing here: even though you are hearing just an explanation, the actual joy comes from the thing itself, from the actual G-dliness.

Not only that. The whole *inyan* (matter) of *bina*, even though *bina* is into an explanation, is that you want to understand the actual thing. You are understanding an explanation, but the *ratzon* (will) of *bina*, the *Keser* (crown) of *bina*, is precisely into the actual thing. That is one of the reasons why *bina* has no upper limit and no lower limit. Actually none of the *middos* (attributes) really has an upper or lower limit, but in a way they do, whereas *bina* does not. And *bina* can go, with no limits, both up and down, in a way of a *yesh*.

You see it even going down. When *bina* goes into the physical reality, it goes into it in a way of a *yesh*, until we actually have things like cars and computers. That is from the *bina*. From *chachma* it does not necessarily go in a way of a *yesh*, because *chachma* is a thing of an *ayin* (nothing), and it will not necessarily give you a way to do actual *yesh* things in the physical reality. *Bina* does.

blocks.title: The scientific method is iyun
blocks.text: People think science is a philosophy. It is really a method, a methodology, and the methodology of science is actually *iyun* (close analysis). You make a theory, a *sevara* (a line of reasoning), and then you test it, just like they do in the Talmud. They make a *sevara*: "Maybe it's like this. So how would that apply to that thing?" "Wait, it seems to work." And then another guy says, "No, look at this," and he blows up your *sevara*. The same thing with science. You come up with a theory and test it against the actual facts of reality, to see if things really work according to your theory. That is what a scientific experiment is: you build up a set of things that will test your theory against actual facts. So the whole scientific method is a thing of *iyun*, of analysis.

And the scientific theory is basically one of the expressions of the eighth king of *Tohu* (the world of Chaos): a *bina* of *Tohu*, a *bina* which is unconnected to G-d. And yet, as they say, the eighth king does not die. We see that the scientists themselves, who started off in the 19th century very full of themselves, sure they had disproved that there is a G-d and stuff like that, the more they get into it, the more they see that there seems to be a Controller of the universe.

blocks.text: The basic thing is that *bina* is into the actual thing, as you see that *bina* into the physical world is into the actual thing. And the same right now: we are just hearing a bunch of explanations, but we are not even really trying to understand how the world came into being. That too is a *mashal* (analogy). What we are really trying to understand is what G-d is, and what we are doing here. That is what *Chassidus* is about.

But **"they will rejoice in You"** is in the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) *mamash*. Right now we are getting a joy from learning. Our joy is not from the fact that it is such an intricate, detailed study, or that we are getting to understand psychology or something like that. If it were just an intricate, detailed study, "I could come up with more intricate, detailed studies." We could study quantum mechanics, and "I wouldn't get a *simcha*; as a matter of fact, I would get bored."

So if you want to call every night, there must be a *taanug* there, a joy and a *taanug*. Where is that coming from?

People have these philosophy groups, you know: they get together and *hak a tchainik* (Yiddish: bang a kettle, chatter on). They will even have a philosophy group or a politics group where they discuss communism, even though they're all Republicans, and they get a whole big joy and *taanug* out of the intricacies of the explanations. The joy of that *bina* comes out of the beauty of the explanation. That is not what is happening here.

blocks.title: An explanation is an elegant building
blocks.text: An explanation is a *binyan*, a building: an elegant structure. When you look at this beautiful, elegant structure of the explanation... Some people like to do mathematical problems, not because they need to do the problem to come up with a certain solution, but because they love to go through these elegant structures of mathematics. Like the old ancient Arabs and the Greeks, the original people who came up with algebra and things like that: it was not so much a matter of *bina*; they got the joy and the *taanug* out of the elegance of the structure itself. What he is telling you is that the joy of *Chassidus* does not come out of the elegance of the structure. It comes out of the G-dliness, because that is the actual subject.

blocks.question: So is "they will rejoice in You" a positive comprehension of what the Aibershter is, the thing we are trying to make contact with?
blocks.text: Not contact: that is what we are trying to understand, in a way of a *yesh*. Maybe not right now; right now it is not an actual comprehension. But later on he will actually promise "we will exult and rejoice in You", *mamash*. When *Moshiach* comes, we will have it.

blocks.text: Why is *bina* into the *etzem* (the essence) of the thing? Because *bina* really has the power to grasp the *etzem*, precisely because it is the *yesh*; and because *bina* is connected to all the levels of *bina*. The whole thing of *bina* is that it goes up and up and up, and down and down and down. So the intellect, even though it is an intellect, when it goes down into the physical world, catches the actual physical world, to the point where it is not just a theory of a car anymore: you can actually make a car. The theory that you can have a combustion engine and a wheel and put them together finally grasps the thing.

blocks.text: The thing of *bina* is grasping. ("Comprehension?" "Not comprehension, grasping. To hold on to the thing.") In Hebrew, *litfos*: as he says in another place, he thinks in chapter one, the *ba'al bina* is called a *tafsan* (a grasper). He is *tofes*, he takes hold of, the actual *etzem* of the thing, so that the *bina* of the physical nature of the world finally grasps the actual thing, and you can make actual changes in actual physical things.

blocks.title: "I don't understand my children"
blocks.text: To understand architecture, or the engineering of how to build a car, aerodynamics, is just intellectual. Nonetheless he does not want just to understand the theory of aerodynamics; he wants to understand how the physical world actually works. When somebody is really trying to understand something, say somebody says, "I don't understand my children," it is because he wants to understand them; and more than understand them, to a point where he can make a change in them, to actually control their behavior. "I don't mean control necessarily in a bad way," but to affect their behavior. Or somebody says, "I would like to understand politics." Some people are not really interested in the *etzem* of the thing, only in the *bina* itself. But that is not the real *inyan* of *bina*. The real *inyan* of *bina* is that you are trying to understand the thing itself.

phrases.he: ולפי הנזכר לעיל דבהשגה לית מחשבה תפיסא ביה,
phrases.en: But according to what was said above, that in comprehension no thought grasps Him at all;

phrases.he: אדרבה מופלא בהפלאת הערך הנבדל כו'
phrases.en: on the contrary, He is wondrous, with the wondrousness of what is separate and beyond compare;

phrases.he: והיינו בבחינת כח מ''ה דחכמה בהעלם כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and this is in the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, hidden, as said above.

blocks.text: **But according to what was said above**, in the last chapter, the thought of *bina* actually does not catch Him. On the contrary: it is totally separate, a totally wondrous thing, so that you see it is wondrous and makes no sense at all. And not just wondrous according to our measure: **beyond compare**, totally non-comparable to anything we can think of.

This is precisely in the *koach MaH* of *chachma* (the power of *chachma* that sees what a thing is). It is not just that when you look into the *bina*, the *bina* itself shows you that some details are missing. There is more than that: from the power of *chachma* you can actually see that there is a wondrous thing, a fantastically wondrous thing, that the *bina* is not describing. That comes from the *koach MaH*, which comes precisely from the overview of the whole thing. When you take in the overview of the whole thing, you see that all the particulars are missing something; and not only that they are missing it, you actually have a sight of it. You see into the actual *mahus* (what it is in itself) of the thing, and that it is totally *nivdal*, separate, from what the explanation is talking about.

Is it in a way of *shlila*, negation? No. The way of negation is in *bina*. The comprehension of *bina* into the thing is by way of negation, but the comprehension, or the sight, of *chachma* is *mamash* like seeing the thing: a positive thing that you see. It comes from the negation of *bina*: the power of *chachma* is awakened by the power of *bina*, and from its negation. There is deductive logic, inductive logic, and another kind of logic. Deductive logic basically says: this, therefore that. You bring up various *pratim* (particulars) and come to a conclusion. That is a comprehension, not of negation, of what the conclusion actually is.

blocks.title: The red ball in one of twenty pockets
blocks.text: *Hasagas hashlila* (comprehension by negation) is like this. There are 20 people in the room, and one of them has got a red ball in his pocket, and we know that. We check 19 people, and they don't have a red ball in their pocket. Now this is almost deductive logic, not a real negation, but it is the beginning of the explanation of what *hasagas hashlila* is. You don't really know that he has a red ball in his pocket; you didn't look in his pocket. Well, it must be him, because it's not them.

blocks.title: Who controls your stomach?
blocks.text: Who is controlling your stomach? You know that it is not you, because sometimes your stomach goes out of control and you can't put it back into control. If you're all full, and then somebody brings a fantastic dish that you love, and you want to make yourself hungry, you can't do it. You have nothing to do with your stomach, so you have to say that it must be G-d who controls it. But you don't have a comprehension of exactly how G-d controls your stomach. That is *hasagas hashlila*.

blocks.title: The palace in the forest
blocks.text: In general, *hasagas hashlila* is what you are compelled to when you look around. This is one of the *meshalim* (analogies) they give that there must be a creator of the world. You come into a palace in the middle of the forest, with a whole bunch of things there, food in the refrigerator. You can't say, "Wow, I wonder how this palace came here out of nothingness in the middle of the forest? I wonder how many billions of years it took till the stones fell into the shape of a palace?" You say, "What do you mean? What are you talking about?" You have to say it is somebody's palace: there has to be a *ba'al habayis* (an owner) to this *bira* (palace). But you don't see the owner. That, in a way, is *hasagas hashlila*: the first level of it.

Then another level of *hasagas hashlila*, the real thing of it, is that you can't figure out what the thing is, but you can figure out what it isn't. That is what the *Rambam* (Maimonides) talks about. The first, even though it is *hasagas hashlila*, is really deductive logic: this, therefore that. If you don't know for sure that somebody really has the ball, you don't know for sure that the 20th guy has it in his pocket; it follows only if you are told for sure that one of them has a ball in his pocket. (The side ends here.)

So you can't really figure out what the *Aibershter* is, but you can figure out that He is not Jesus. He is not a person. "So what is it? If you know so good, so what is it?" "What it is, the actual *mahus*, you can't figure out. But I can tell you what it's not." That is the real *hasagas hashlila*. But that is a comprehension: not in *chachma*, but the actual form of logic, by which you can actually figure out what the thing is not.

blocks.title: The mountain that keeps getting bigger
blocks.text: And what it sees in the *mahus* is not really so much what it is, just how far removed it is. It is like walking towards a big, big mountain. It looks like a big mountain, and you say, "Wow, must be about a mile away. That's a really big mountain." You're walking and walking, you already walked three miles, and now the mountain looks much bigger. "Wait a minute, this mountain was a lot bigger than I thought. It wasn't a mile away: we already walked three miles, and now it looks maybe five miles away." You keep walking, and it gets bigger and bigger and looks farther and farther. "Wait a minute, how big is this mountain? How far away from it are we?" And the more you keep walking, the bigger and farther it gets.

blocks.title: The mountain that keeps getting bigger
blocks.text: So you get a bigger and bigger sense of *hafla'a* (wondrousness), and then the sense of *hafla'a* does a double take. All of a sudden it hits you: it's not even a hundred miles, and not that big. "I have no idea how big it is or how far away it is. That I see it at a certain size and a certain distance is just an imagination, a mirage." That is the real *hafla'a* of the *Aibershter*: not the *hafla'a* you get from seeing how big it is, but starting to realize that you are making a whole mistake, and it will just keep going like that; no matter how much you travel, it will keep getting bigger and farther.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 065 is a free discussion that reads no line; it opens by finishing the point on comprehension by negation that class 064 ended on.

blocks.text: So even the *hafla'a* is not unconnected to *bina*: as we said before, there is no *bina* without *chachma* and no *chachma* without *bina*. The sense of *hafla'a* actually comes from the *hasagas hashlila*. But the sense of *hafla'a* is a positive thing: you actually see the *hafla'a*. The *hasagas hashlila* is a comprehension of *bina* that says, "Well, it's none of these things," and from this comes the sense of *hafla'a* of *chachma*.

phrases.he: ואם כן נהפוך הוא,
phrases.en: If so, it is the reverse:

phrases.he: שאין השמחה במהותו כו'
phrases.en: the joy is not in His very being,

phrases.he: כי מאחר שמשיג,
phrases.en: for since he comprehends,

phrases.he: אין זה אמיתתו ומהותו,
phrases.en: it is not His truth and His being,

phrases.he: רק בחינת צמצומו להוות המתהווה כו'
phrases.en: only His *tzimtzum* (contraction), to bring into being what comes into being;

phrases.he: ובחכמה, בחינת אין כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: and in *chachma*, the aspect of *ayin*, as said above,

phrases.he: שם ראוי להיות השמחה, כמו שאמר וישמחו בך
phrases.en: there the joy should be, as it says, "they will rejoice in You."

phrases.he: ואינו כן כידוע,
phrases.en: And it is not so, as is known,

phrases.he: דהביטול היפך, השמחה
phrases.en: for the *bittul* is the opposite of joy,

phrases.he: בחכמה דווקא
phrases.en: [and is] precisely in *chachma*,

phrases.he: והשמחה בבינה כו'
phrases.en: and the joy is in *bina*.

blocks.text: **And it is not so**: the *bittul* is actually the opposite of joy. In *bittul* you feel like you're nothing.

blocks.title: The wedding and the Cossacks
blocks.text: Whereas joy, the whole thing of joy, is precisely like when he's at a wedding, and he drank a bunch of booze, and he's jumping around: that's joy. The whole thing of joy is like a bunch of Cossacks: they feel they're something. Everybody is dancing and knocking everybody else on the back and stuff like that. That's joy, right? Whereas the *bittul* is actually the opposite of joy, and it is in *chachma*; and the joy is in *bina*. So what's going on here?

sections.title: Everything has its opposite: one power in two equal lines
sections.summary: A thing's whole power comes from its opposite, as delight and pain measure each other: one power divided into two equal lines. So the push of *bina* comes from not understanding, and its real object is the Essence, which is the most not-understandable of all.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא
phrases.en: But the explanation is

phrases.he: כידוע שבכל דבר יש היפוכו,
phrases.en: as is known: in everything there is also its opposite;

phrases.he: וגם שנגלה להיפוכו ממש,
phrases.en: and even though it appears to be *mamash* its opposite,

phrases.he: אדרבה מזה עצמו
phrases.en: on the contrary, from this itself

phrases.he: נראה לעין שכל כחו אינו בא רק מכח המנגדו ממש
phrases.en: it is seen that its whole power comes only from the power of its opposite, *mamash*.

blocks.text: **But the explanation is**, as is known: in everything there is also its opposite. And even though it appears to be *mamash* its total opposite, from the very fact that it is its total opposite we see that its whole power comes precisely from the opposite.

What he means here is that the power of understanding comes from not understanding. The whole push of understanding is when you don't understand something: that is what pushes you to want to understand. It is precisely the not understanding that pushes you to understand, so the push to understand is to understand what you don't understand.

So in understanding itself, in *bina*, he is saying not only that the *bina* of *Chassidus* is into *Elokus* (G-dliness). He is saying that the whole thing of *bina* is precisely into *Elokus*, because that is the most non-understandable thing. Other things, you could say, "Well, those could be understood." This is not just that you don't understand it: it is non-understandable. So the whole push of *bina*, and the real *inyan* of *bina*, is precisely the *bina* into *Elokus* itself, because that is its exact opposite.

phrases.he: ולפי ערך כח המנגד כן ימצא כח היפוכו ממש,
phrases.en: According to the measure of the power of the opposite, so will the power of its opposite be found, *mamash*;

phrases.he: אם כן כדבר אחד ממש הוא
phrases.en: if so, it is *mamash* like one thing.

blocks.text: **According to the measure of the power of the opposite**, so is the power of the thing. It is like this in the *sefarim* (the books) too, with delight and pain, weeping and joy. According to how much you miss somebody, that's how much you want him to be there, and how happy you'll be when he's there. It is precisely the power of the opposite that gives the thing its power. **if so, it is *mamash* like one thing**.

phrases.he: כמו הענג והצער,
phrases.en: Like delight and pain:

phrases.he: שלפי ערך כח התענוג בדבר מה,
phrases.en: according to the measure of the power of the delight in something,

phrases.he: כן ממש לפי ערך ימצא כח התפעלות הצער,
phrases.en: so, *mamash*, in that measure, will be found the power of the feeling of pain,

phrases.he: שהוא גרעון אור הענג המנגדו
phrases.en: which is the lack of the light of the delight that opposes it;

phrases.he: דהיינו אם יעמוד לנגדו דבר לבטל הענג ההוא
phrases.en: that is, if something stands against him to cancel that delight,

phrases.he: להיות מן ההיפוך כו'
phrases.en: to be the opposite.

phrases.he: וכן להיפך,
phrases.en: And so the reverse:

phrases.he: ערך הענג מדבר מה לא יוכר רק לפי ערך הצער בהעדר אותו הדבר כו'
phrases.en: the measure of the delight in something is recognized only by the measure of the pain in the absence of that thing.

blocks.text: **Like delight and pain**: according to the power of the delight in something, so will be the power of the pain, the lack of the delight; and that is how much you are going to want the thing. If something will prevent him from having it, that is how much pain he is going to have, according to how much delight he had. **And so the reverse**: exactly the same.

So it is *mamash* one power, and the understanding is actually the non-understanding: the whole power of understanding comes from not understanding. Say, as it were, that we understood this better than the Mitteler Rebbe (the author). Then we wouldn't read this book. The whole reason we are reading this book is that we don't understand it. So the actual power of *bina* is the power of not understanding. That's the whole thing.

Think about it in anything. You see somebody trying to understand something real hard: he's working, he's doing *bina*, doing *hisbonenus*, thinking about it. What does it mean? That he doesn't understand it. So the real power of *bina*, in a way more than all the other *sefiros*, is *Atzmus Elokus* (the Essence of G-dliness). The power of *bina* is *mamash* rooted there, because that is the ununderstandable, the totally ununderstandable thing there is. *Bina* is rooted in *Elokus* in a way more than anything else, because *Elokus* is the total antithesis of *bina*. That's what *Elokus* is: the total ununderstandable.

In love or fear it is not the total antithesis. Even in *chachma*, you see that it is not really the opposite of *chachma*: in a way it is, to a certain extent, but not like *bina*. In *bina* it is *mamash* the total antithesis, the total opposite. So what *bina* really is, is *atzmuso umahuso*, His Essence and being, which is its opposite. Of all the things you can't understand, that is the thing you can most not understand: not that you don't understand it yet but could, but *mamash* totally non-understandable. It is so in *bina* even more than in *chachma*. In *chachma* you can have a flash, an intuitive thing into *Elokus* (not that it is actually into *Elokus*), so it is still not the total opposite. But what he is telling you here is that the Essence is *bina*. That's what the Essence is.

phrases.he: הרי כח אחד הוא ממש,
phrases.en: So it is *mamash* one power,

phrases.he: רק שנחלק לב' קווין שוין ממש ושקולין
phrases.en: only divided into two lines, *mamash* equal, and weighing the same,

phrases.he: בלתי יטה כח קו א' על ב' אפילו כקוצו של יו״ד
phrases.en: the power of one line not tilting over the second even by the tip of a *yud*.

blocks.text: **So it is *mamash* one power**. The Essence is the totally non-understandable, and since it is the opposite, that is the power of *bina*: the actual power of *bina* is the Essence, what you can't understand. As we said, the power that drives somebody to understand something is the fact that he doesn't understand it.

blocks.question: But when someone knows that something is unattainable, doesn't he give up hope of it?
blocks.text: It depends how much *taanug* there is in it. That is not really true. Look at a heroin addict: he knows that he can't get that first high anymore, but he's still trying, because of the *taanug*. True, the pain can put him into a melancholy, so that he'll stop trying. That is because of melancholy, *atzvus*. But that is the whole thing he explains: you are supposed to have *marirus* (bitterness), not *atzvus*. *Marirus* is the opposite power that precisely drives you.

**only divided into two lines, *mamash* equal**: two equal lines going in two different directions, weighing exactly the same, **not tilting** one over the other even like a dot. So the pain and the delight are exactly the same; and the same thing, the not understanding and the drive to understand are exactly the same. So the drive to understand is the strongest in *Elokus*, more than anything else, to the point that you can say that the actual *mahus* of *bina* is the *mahus* of the *Aibershter*.

If you look very closely, the *mahus* of *bina* into anything else, wanting to understand your children, wanting to understand psychology, finally comes down to one thing: what you really want to understand is *Elokus*. And that, of course, is why the eighth king does not die. No matter what he is trying to understand, the real thing he is trying to understand is precisely *Elokus*. So he can't really become disconnected. Even if he is disconnected for a while, because *bina* can get hung up in the details, it doesn't matter: its real essence is precisely into *Elokus*. That's what he really wants to know. **even by the tip of a *yud***: not even like a dot.

sections.title: Joy and weeping in bina, and in the hidden delight of chachma
sections.summary: The more one has tasted G-dliness in comprehension, the more one weeps over its hiding, to the point of disgust with one's life; and above that, the hidden delight of *chachma* brings a *bittul* that throws away everything that feels itself. In each, the two lines weigh the same; and *bina*, which grasps nothing of the Essence, is the most opposite and so the most bound to it.

phrases.he: וכן החדווה והבכיה,
phrases.en: So too joy and weeping:

phrases.he: שלפי ערך החדווה,
phrases.en: according to the measure of the joy,

phrases.he: שהוא ענג המורגש בגלוי אלקות בהשגתו כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: which is the felt delight in the revelation of G-dliness in his comprehension, as said above,

phrases.he: כך ימצא קו הב' שיוצא ממנו ומכחו דוקא
phrases.en: so will be found the second line, which comes out of it and from its power precisely,

blocks.text: **So too joy and weeping**: exactly according to how much he enjoys his comprehension of the revelation of G-dliness, exactly according to that will be **the second line**, the weeping over the absence of the revelation of the light in his soul, because G-dliness is hidden. The weeping is precisely according to how much you understand. So the more *Chassidus* you learn, the more you are going to be bothered about what you don't understand, because it is in proportion. A guy who doesn't understand nothing, it doesn't bother him at all. Precisely a guy who knows a whole bunch of *Chassidus* will be totally bothered, until he is, as it says, *mamash* disgusted with his life: in his life, all this is worth nothing.

Say they tell him, "Ah, what if we make you Bill Gates, and you'll be a super zillionaire, but you'll have to give up *Chassidus*?" There's no way, man. Not possible. He can't even stand the whole life and the whole world. He says, "I can't take this world. *Moshiach* has to come, so that we'll be able to sit and study the whole time" (and not get tired), and the whole time will be just one giant *farbrengen* (a Chassidic gathering). Because *farbrengen* means you study *Chassidus*: that is the real thing, as you see by the Rebbe. A *farbrengen* means you study, and eat, and sleep, and everything is right there at the table; and even the song you sing in between the *maamarim* (discourses) is all part of the *Chassidus*.

phrases.he: שהוא הבכיה על העדר גלוי האור בנפשו
phrases.en: which is the weeping over the absence of the revelation of the light in his soul,

phrases.he: מצד הסתר אלהו״ת, עד שמואס בחייו ממש
phrases.en: because G-dliness is hidden, until he is *mamash* disgusted with his life.

blocks.text: **until he is *mamash* disgusted with his life**, till he says, "I can't take my life anymore. Every day I have to go to work, and I have to do this and that. *Moshiach* has to come." It is like the ruling of the *Rambam* in *halacha*: why did they want *Moshiach*? Not because of all the external things, the delicacies, which are like dust; but because it will give them the time to study *Chassidus*.

phrases.he: וכל שטעם טעם ענג אלה״י בחדווה יותר,
phrases.en: The more he has tasted the taste of G-dly delight in joy,

phrases.he: יותר יתמרמר בנפשו מהיפוכו
phrases.en: the more he will be embittered in his soul by its opposite.

phrases.he: וכן להיפך,
phrases.en: And so the reverse:

phrases.he: מערך עומק המרירות והבכיה למאוס בחייו הגשמים,
phrases.en: from the measure of the depth of the bitterness and the weeping, to be disgusted with his physical life,

phrases.he: ניכר ערך כח העונג והחדווה באלהו״ת, כמה ערך כוחו
phrases.en: is recognized the measure of the power of the delight and joy in G-dliness, how great its power is;

phrases.he: כי ב' קווין הללו שקולין מאד בשווה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: for these two lines weigh very much the same, as said above,

phrases.he: והיינו בכיה מסטרא דא וחדוה מסטרא דא בשקול אחד בשווה ממש
phrases.en: that is, weeping on one side and joy on the other, in one equal balance, *mamash*.

blocks.text: **The more he has tasted the taste of G-dly delight in joy**, the more bitter he will be over its opposite. Somebody who never tasted a steak doesn't long for it. **And so the reverse**: when he totally cannot take his physical life anymore, from that you can see how much pleasure he is getting in *Elokus*, how strong it is. Why? **for these two lines weigh very much the same**, *mamash* equal: **weeping on one side and joy on the other**.

phrases.he: וכמו כן למעלה מזה בבחינת עונג הנעלם שבחכמה,
phrases.en: And so too, higher than this, in the hidden delight that is in *chachma*,

phrases.he: שמזה בא בחינת הביטול מעצמותו לגמרי,
phrases.en: from which comes the *bittul* from his very self, completely

phrases.he: (בל"א צו טראגן גאר פון זיך)
phrases.en: (in Yiddish, *tzu tragen gor fun zich*, to be carried right away from oneself),

phrases.he: מעומק עונג הנעלם בעצמיות שלו כו'
phrases.en: from the depth of the hidden delight in his own very self;

phrases.he: הרי היפוכו הבא מכחו
phrases.en: its opposite, which comes from its power,

phrases.he: הוא ענין השלכת נפשו מנגד בכל דבר המנגד לזה,
phrases.en: is throwing his life away against anything that opposes this,

phrases.he: שהוא נכלל בבחינת הרגשת עצמו
phrases.en: which is included in the feeling of himself;

phrases.he: דהיינו למאוס בחייו בתכלית התבטלות האמיתית,
phrases.en: that is, to be disgusted with his life, in the utmost true self-nullification,

phrases.he: כמו מי לי בשמים ועמך כו' כלה כו'
phrases.en: as in "Whom do I have in heaven, and with You [I want nothing on earth]... [my flesh and my heart] fail."

blocks.text: The same thing **higher than this, in the hidden delight that is in *chachma***, from which comes a *bittul* from his very self, completely: he doesn't even know he's there anymore. In Yiddish, *tzu tragen gor fun zich*: he's totally gone from himself. It is from the hidden delight in the Essence, from the flash of the *hafla'a*.

**its opposite, which comes from its power**, is that he will totally throw his life away against anything that will stop him from this; and that is everything **included in the feeling of himself**: anything that will make him feel himself.

That is, to be totally disgusted with his life: "Whom do I have in heaven", what do I have to do with anything in heaven, "and with You I want nothing on earth", what do I want from anything on earth? Other than You. Don't bother me with heaven, and don't bother me with earth: I want only *Chassidus*. "My flesh and my heart fail": I have nothing to do with my emotions, and I have nothing to do with my meat.

phrases.he: כי ב' קווין שקולים בשווה הן כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.
phrases.en: For the two lines weigh the same, as said above; and this is enough for one who understands.

blocks.text: **For the two lines weigh the same**: the delight and the weeping are *mamash* the same thing. And what he is basically saying here is that in *chachma* too, the *chachma* is precisely into the Essence. Why? Because the whole thing of *chachma* is that he feels that he doesn't have it: it's the *hafla'a*. But the main thing of that is precisely in *bina*. The matter of *chachma* is precisely the *ayin*, so the fact that he doesn't have it is what *chachma* is; it is not a total negation. It is precisely in *bina* that it is a total negation of it.

The same with *chesed* (kindness), for instance: there is a negation there, which is why the *chesed* is precisely into the Essence. The real love is precisely into the Essence, because he feels that it is impossible to love G-d properly. But he can love G-d a little bit. In *bina* he can't understand G-d at all. Even with all the explanations and everything, he feels that he is not understanding G-d a little bit: he is not understanding G-d at all, totally. It is a total lack.

In all the other things there is also the opposite, and that is the real *inyan* of all the *middos* as we understand them. "What do you mean, the *bina* comes from *Elokus* and the other *middos* don't?" We know that all the *middos* come from *Elokus*, and it says He is *mikol ilein middos*, the opposite of all the *middos*. But nothing like *bina*. And that is why the whole thing is *bina sheb'bina* (*bina* within *bina*): because that is the strongest power into *Elokus*.

blocks.text: So the thing about *bina*: it is a very special *sefira*, because, as we said, *bina* is precisely into the Essence. The lack of the thing is a *kaf shakul*, a pan of the scale weighing the same as the thing: the opposite of the thing weighs the same as the thing. You see the difference between *bina* and all the other *sefiros* in a couple of ways. One of them is that precisely in *bina*, the lack of *bina* causes you to want to have *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: In the other *sefiros* it is not necessarily like that. The lack of *ratzon* for something does not make you want to want it. The lack of *taanug* in something makes you, just the opposite, not want to have a *taanug* in it. Even the lack of *chachma*, which is *bittul*: the lack of *bittul* does not make you want *bittul*. And the lack of love or hatred does not make you have it. The only one that is a little like that, not quite the same as *bina*, is *netzach* (victory): if you're losing, you want to win. But that is only in a person who already has the *midda* of *netzach*. A person who is not ambitious (ambition is the *midda* of *netzach*) is not made to want ambition by his lack of ambition, even though a person who is losing wants to win. That is really basically in all the *middos*: once you have the *midda*, the lack of it makes you want more of it.

blocks.text: But the thing is, in *bina* you see that even a stupid person who's not a *bina* type of person... You say, wait a minute, doesn't that apply in *bina* too? A non-ambitious person is not trying to be an ambitious person, so a non-intellectual person is not trying to become an intellectual; just the opposite, he thinks they're all eggheads and stuff like that. But you see that it's not true. Every person, no matter how stupid he is, wants to be a *mevin* (one who understands). Like the kind of people around here: if you talk to them, they'll tell you why the Steelers lost. The quarterback made that play wrong, he should have done it like that, and they'll give you a whole analysis. And then they feel like they're a *mevin*.

blocks.title: The snake's new names
blocks.text:
There is the thing from the Mitteler Rebbe. A man came to him and said that he has a *hargashas hayesh*, a feeling of his own existence. The Rebbe asked him, "You know what *hargashas hayesh* means?" The man was smart enough to just shut up. So the Rebbe said, "Let me tell you a story."

Originally there was the primordial snake, and he had a job to do. After *Adam HaRishon* realized what had happened, the snake came crying to the *Aibershter*: "Nobody's going to listen to me. They see the primordial snake, they won't listen to me. They're scared of a snake." The *Aibershter* said, "Don't worry, don't worry, I'll give you a new name," and He gave him a new name: the *Satan*. This worked for many years, and everything was fine. Then people started finding out about the *Satan*, and nobody wanted to listen to him. He came crying to the *Aibershter*: "How can I do my job? Nobody wants to listen to the *Satan*." "Don't worry, I'll give you a new name": and He called him the *yetzer hara* (the evil inclination).

blocks.title: The snake's new names
blocks.text: This worked for many, many years; Rabbi Markel thinks he said it was good until the days of the Baal Shem Tov, or something like that ("I can't remember the exact dates he gave; he gave a date for everything, when it changed over"). Then he came over and said, "Nobody wants to listen to the *yetzer hara* anymore." "Don't worry, I'll give you a new name: the *yesh*." And it worked out. Finally, in the days of the Mitteler Rebbe or the Alter Rebbe, or whatever (he does not remember who the cutoffs were; he thinks it was the Baal Shem Tov who let them know about the *yesh*), he said, "Everybody knows about the *yesh* already." "I'll give you a new name: the *hargashas hayesh*." And, the Rebbe said, you should realize: the *hargashas hayesh*, that's the *yesh*, that's the *yetzer hara*, that's the *Satan*, that's the primordial snake.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: So the *yesh* is the primordial snake, where it says that *chachma* is an *ayin* and *bina* is a *yesh*. Not only that: the whole *yesh* comes from the left side of *bina*. The whole *yesh* of something comes from *bina*. And not only that: as far as the *ayin* upstairs, it is the light that is called the *ayin*. The *Or Ein Sof* is called the *ayin*, and the Essence is called the *yesh ha'amiti*, the true *yesh*. So both the good and the bad all come out of *bina*. All the *kelipos* (husks) come out of *bina*. Everything comes out of *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: So the only one that is a little bit the same is *netzach*: by *netzach*, if you're losing, you want to win. But first of all, *netzach* is only by somebody who already has the *midda* of *netzach*; somebody who is not ambitious doesn't want to be ambitious. But somebody who doesn't understand wants to understand, and the whole ego of people, the whole *yesh* of people, is to show that he's a *mevin* in whatever it is. And then there is another thing that even *netzach* doesn't have: what he said, that *bina* is the farthest away from the Essence. When it comes to understanding, you don't understand nothing about the Essence. The whole understanding is precisely into how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*, not into the Essence.

blocks.text: Whereas everything else, like *taanug* and *ratzon*: the *taanug* and *ratzon* are not as much into the Essence as they should be, but still a little bit. The same with *chachma*, which is *bittul*, the feeling of *hafla'a*. It is not as much as it should be; but even somebody who doesn't understand that much (as we said, according to the *bina* is the *chachma*), even a regular person, still has a little bit of *hafla'a* toward the *Aibershter*. He is *modeh*, he acknowledges: that is why he calls Him the *Aibershter*, which means He is higher. So there is a little bit of *hafla'a*.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: And the same thing with *daas* (knowledge), which means connection. Some people are very connected, some people are not very connected; they are not as connected as they should be, but there is still a little bit of connection. The same thing with love: none of us love the *Aibershter* how we should, but there is still a certain amount of love, and a certain amount of fear. And *netzach* is a thing of overcoming your bad habits and stuff like that in order to get closer to the *Aibershter*: nobody is really that great with *netzach* like they should be, but in everybody there is at least a little bit of overcoming. And the same with *hoda'a* (acknowledgement): everybody acknowledges to some extent... (the side ends here).

blocks.text: (The side begins in mid-sentence.) Even then it doesn't matter: 98 or 99.99, it is not 100%. Negligible means that there is a little bit there, but it is *batel* (nullified): *batel* in sixty, *batel* in a thousand, *batel* in a million, but still really there. It is as it says, *kula kamei k'la chashiv*, everything before Him is considered as nothing: in front of the *Aibershter* it is as if it doesn't exist. And in front of the *Aibershter* it is not like *batel* in sixty, which is a kind of an error. It is *batel* like 1 over infinity. If you say that 1 over infinity is 0, it's not really true. The 1 is still a 1; it is just that compared to infinity it is negligible, as if it's a 0.

blocks.title: One over infinity is not zero
blocks.text: When people say 1 over infinity is 0, it's not really true, because they don't know mathematics. There is no such real mathematical formula. The actual formula is like this: 1 over 2 is a half, 1 over 3 is a third, 1 over 4 is a quarter; as the numbers on the bottom get bigger and approach infinity, the numbers get smaller and smaller, more and more negligible, and approach 0. But it is not actually there. It is not actually 0, because 1 is still 1.

blocks.title: Spit in the vodka
blocks.text: They were talking about real *Yiddishkeit* and diluted *Yiddishkeit* (a student: "this is kind of like Zeno's paradox"). A guy was telling Shimon: so what's the big deal if you dilute it with a little bit of water? If you take vodka and put a little water in it, it's still vodka; it's just slightly weaker. So Rabbi Markel told Shimon to tell him: "What if I'll give you a glass of vodka and I'll spit in it? I'll spit in your vodka." You know what I mean?

blocks.title: The ocean
blocks.text: But in the ocean, if I'm standing next to you in the ocean, you don't care: to the ocean it's already negligible. Even if you have rotten fish in it, to the ocean it's negligible. But it's not that it's not there; it's still there. Whatever amount of fecal matter the fishies made is totally there, all of it. The absolute amount is there; it is just *k'la chashiv*, considered as nothing. That is what *kula kamei k'la chashiv* means: there is a *kaf* there, *k'la*, *like* nothing.

blocks.text: But *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him) is a different thing. *Ein od milvado* means 100% pure alcohol: not even one molecule of water in it, and not one molecule of anything else, not one molecule of dust, not one molecule of sodium. It's pure. There's nothing else here. And there are actually two things that are *ein od milvado*. There is the *Aibershter*: the actual Essence, or *mahus*. And there is one other thing: *bina*. In *bina* there is not one iota of understanding into the Essence. It is not that it is just negligible: as he said, if you understand, it is not into the Essence. That is what we learned yesterday: if you understand anything at all, it is not into the Essence. That is precisely why *bina* will take you to the Essence. So *bina* is the complete opposite of the Essence, and the Essence is the complete opposite of *bina*, exactly the same.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.text: In *chachma* and *ratzon* and everything else it is not like that. As we said, there is a little bit of *ratzon* into the Essence, so there is a little bit of the Essence in the *ratzon*: a *ratzon* is actually that you want the Essence. And the *chachma*, the *bittul*, the *hafla'a*: as he says here, the *hafla'a* is from the Essence, not from the coming into being of the *yesh* from the *ayin*. Obviously the amount of *hafla'a* that we have into the Essence, or even a big guy has, is... "Well, how much *hafla'a* is it?" "It's *k'la chashiv*, like nothing." Compared to the Essence it's nothing, and compared to how much *hafla'a* he really should have it's nothing; but there is still a little bit there.

blocks.text: The same thing with love. Even Avraham Avinu said, "I am dust and ashes," and *Chassidus*, the *Tanya*, explains what he meant: it is a *mashal*. When you burn a big tree, there is nothing left but a little bit of dust and ashes. So, compared to the *middos* of *chesed* of *Atzilus*, Avraham's *chesed* is like dust and ashes compared to the actual tree. It's as if the tree is gone and nothing is there; but it is not really nothing: there is dust and ashes. And the same with everything else. *Netzach* also: you overcame a little bit. *Hod*: you are *modeh*, not like you should be. And *Malchus*: he does not accept the yoke of the kingship of Heaven 100%, but a little bit is there.

blocks.text: But in *bina*, this is what he said: if there is a little bit of *bina* there, it means it is not into the Essence. If there is any kind of understanding, it means it is not into the Essence. So *bina* is the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.question: Does this have something to do with the depth above and the depth below, omek rom and omek tachas?
blocks.text: It has very much to do with them: that is the next thing he was going to get to. The *omek rom*, the depth above, is the *yesh ha'amiti*, the true *yesh*; and the *omek tachas*, the depth below, is the *yesh hagamur*, the complete *yesh*. Read the *maamar* of the Mitteler Rebbe called *Ata Echad*: he says that the revelation of the true *yesh* is precisely in the complete *yesh*. And what is the complete *yesh*? Precisely a person who understands. As he said, from the understanding you get a *yeshus*, a sense of self, and a joy, to the point where he is like drunk. It says *bina* is wine: "wine gladdens the heart of man" is *bina*, and the heart too, *bina liba*, *bina* is the heart. Wine is the secrets of the Torah, *bina*; and then there are the secrets of the secrets, *bina sheb'bina*: *Chassidus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.text: The *hisbonenus* of *Chassidus* is called vodka, *mashke*: in many places they call it *mashke*. Even the songs: "Don't you worry, guys, what's going to happen to our lives, we're going to end up in Las Vegas, we'll have some vodka, too." They didn't say Las Vegas, they said a Russian equivalent. (Mendy said it's Kamchatka; the Yiddish is not Kamchatka, it's the *kretchme*, a Russian bar. There are a few versions.) In other words: don't you worry, guys, what's going to happen with us, we're going to end up in the bar and have some vodka, too. And it's a *Chassidish* song. What kind of a *Chassidish* song is that? Because vodka means *Chassidus*. And *Chassidus* is sometimes called *zeks un ninetsiker*, ninety-six proof. That's wrong. Really it's a hundred, *hunderteker*: the real *Chassidus* is 100% alcohol.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.title: The plunger: bina is the biggest vacuum
blocks.text: How can it be 100% alcohol? When your sink is plugged, you get a pump, and you create a vacuum, and the vacuum sucks it in. The biggest vacuum is *bina*. That is what the *Aibershter* says: He can only be in an empty place. If you're there, He can't be there; if there's something there, He won't come there. "What do you mean?" Precisely: the *Aibershter* doesn't want to be there with a *yesh*. If you're a *yesh*, He won't come there. You say, that's a different kind of *yesh*. A *yesh* of *bina* means that it is totally empty of the *Aibershter*: a total vacuum, and that sucks the *Aibershter* in. A 100% lack of understanding is an absolute vacuum, so it sucks Him in totally, in an absolute sort of way.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.text: Other things, like love: a person works on himself, as in the *Chovos HaLevavos* or something like that, to feel that he has a vacuum of love for the *Aibershter*, or a lack of fear, in order to bring the *Aibershter* in. But that is not a 100% vacuum: he still has some. And it is not a vacuum of the Essence, so there is some of the Essence there. And it says about the *etzem* that if you grasp any part of the *etzem*, you grasp the whole *etzem*. So since there is a little bit of the *etzem* there, there is no vacuum: the whole *etzem* is there. In *bina* it is exactly the opposite. That is what he says: if you have any *bina*, there is no Essence there; and if there is any actual Essence there, it is not *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.text: So then he says, "How can it be that precisely *bina*?" Not only that: this goes all the way back to chapter one. Why are we going with *bina*? Why not with *chachma*, or with the *middos*, or whatever? It says, *ha b'ha talya*, one depends on the other: they are *mamash* two equal pans of a scale. And that is precisely where the true *yesh* will come into the complete *yesh*. The real complete *yesh*, as we said, is what the whole *yeshus* of people is: that they understand. When people *shvitz* (boast) around with their *yesh*, what they are boasting about is how much they understand, in whatever stupidity it is.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.title: The Gra: "a convert who converted"
blocks.text: And the other thing he says about boasting: it says, "Let him who praises himself praise himself in this." And you notice what it calls him. There is a thing from the Gra, on the laws of *Pesach*: in the middle of *Pesach*, a minor who grew up, a slave who was freed, and a *ger shenisgayer*, "a convert who converted"; they explain where he becomes obligated immediately, in the middle of *Pesach*. A minor who grew up: before, he was a minor, then he grew up. A slave who was freed: first he was a slave, and then he became a free man. It should have said "a gentile who converted": first he was a gentile, then he became a convert. It doesn't say that. It says "a convert who converted", and from this he deduces that a convert already has the soul of a convert.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.title: Praising himself: hallel and holelus
blocks.text: So here too: how come it says "let him who praises himself", *yis'halel hamis'halel*? That's what it calls him. It says a wise man, a mighty man, a rich man, and then a *mis'halel*. You know what *hallel* is? It's the same root as *holelus*. You know what *holelus* means? (A student: "self-praise.") "No, no, no." There are all sorts of ways to explain this. *Hallel* means praise, and *mis'halel* means he praises himself. But *hallel* also comes from *holelus*, and *holelus* means like a wild party: a wildness, not just a wildness, a wild joy of self-abandonment. ("Like meaningless joy.") It's not just meaningless; the main thing is that it's totally crazy joy. *Holelus* doesn't necessarily mean that the joy is meaningless: there could be a reason for the joy to start off with, but you're not supposed to go into *holelus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.title: Praising himself: hallel and holelus
blocks.text: Even when you have a joy, say it's *Sukkos* or *Pesach*, you're not supposed to just get totally drunk and go into total *holelus*. But here you're allowed to. Not only allowed to: he's called a *mis'halel*. He is doing two things. He's praising himself, *shvitzing*, making himself into a total *yesh*; and he's flipping out, drinking vodka and then throwing up and falling down in it. That's called *holelus*. So how does that apply here? "Let him who praises himself praise himself in this": over here you can have joy without bounds at all, with self-abandonment; you can flip out with joy. That's one thing. And another thing: you can become a total *yesh*. Not only a *yesh* to yourself: you can go around telling everybody, "I am the greatest." As it says, "Praise G-d, all nations"; here he is doing it to himself, like Cassius Clay: "I am the greatest." So that is the whole special thing of *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.text: So *bina* is a special thing. Before, we learned that chapters one, two and three explained that *bina* is special in that all the powers are activated precisely by *bina*, whether the powers above it or the powers below it, and that *bina* can go both up and down. Then chapter 4 basically explained that it is precisely the matter of the *prat* (the particular), which again is precisely *bina*. And then chapter 5 explained that there is no *chachma* without *bina*. You say, yes, but there is no *bina* without *chachma* either. Yes, but the real thing is *bina*. You can't have a *chachma* without the *bina*, because we said in chapter 1 that you can't have a *chachma* just like that, only start to have a *chachma*; but you can have a *bina*. You can be *misbonen* (contemplate), and as a matter of fact that is what *chachma* comes from. And now he is telling us that the *bina* is "we will exult and rejoice in You", *mamash*.

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: And therefore the *omek tachas*, the depth below, is the spring on the *chachma* side. (A student: "Yes, but it's the spring from underground.") It is what stimulates the *chachma*, which is the *bina sheb'bina*. But what stimulates the *chachma* is what *Moshiach* will do: he'll cut open the river, into the depth of the spring, and the whole spring will come straight out into the river. So what are the springs? The "springs of wisdom" are the depth below: we just said that *bina* is the depth below. But it says that the inner core of the inner core of *Abba* (*chachma*) is the inner core of *Atik* (lit. the Ancient of Days).
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: That is what he explains there: the external spring is *chachma*. The aquifer is not *chachma*; the aquifer is *Atik*, and the inner core of *Abba* goes into the inner core of *Atik*. But it also says that the inner core of *bina*, of *Ima* (lit. mother), is the inner core of *Abba*. What is the difference? The inner core of *Abba* is the aquifer inside the aquifer, not outside. And the opening up of the spring comes precisely from *bina*, to bring it out. That is the *ish tevuna*, the man of *tevuna* (drawing an idea out): the *ish tevuna* can draw from the aquifer. That is the whole matter of a well: a well goes into the aquifer, and the *ish tevuna* can draw. Now that is a regular *ish tevuna*. But there can be another kind of *ish tevuna*, who can open up the whole aquifer and bring the whole aquifer out, not in pails. "The springs of wisdom will be opened" does not mean that the *chachma* did it. The *bina* did it: the *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 067 is a free discussion that reads no line; it continues class 066's discussion of bina as the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: Because the springs of wisdom come out drop by drop, through the "hollow and hollowed out", you know. But to open up the whole thing means to bring the depth out to the outside: that is what "will be opened" means. What does the Flood mean? The aquifer came out; it wasn't a depth anymore. And the same with the depth above: the waters from above the heavens came down to the open. And that is done precisely by *bina*: that's what he said in chapter 1, it's the *bina* that does that. The Flood came from *bina*. Why? Because it's not just that he'll reach the aquifer inside the aquifer, but that he opens it up; and not just opens it up, he brings it to the shallowness, out on top of the earth, as happened in the Flood. And then the whole earth will be "filled with the knowledge of G-d as the waters cover the sea", as it was by the Flood: the whole earth was covered with water like the ocean. So that too is *bina*: to bring the aquifers out is a matter of *bina*, and actually of *tevuna*.

blocks.text: (They find the place.) Up to now we learned two kinds of things. The first weeping was over the absence of the revelation of light in his soul, because he doesn't understand, because G-dliness is hidden. The next one is from the hidden delight in *chachma*, from which comes a *bittul* from his very self completely, until he totally cannot stand anything that goes against it: he is disgusted with his life in the utmost true *bittul*. **For the two lines weigh the same**: and that one is of *chachma*.

There is a thing in the year 5708 (*Tashach*): the Frierdiker Rebbe (the previous Rebbe) says that the real *pnimiyus chachma*, the inner core of *chachma*... *Chassidus* says that *pnimiyus chachma* is the *koach MaH* of *chachma*; but he says that is really the outside of the *pnimiyus chachma*. The real *pnimiyus chachma* is where he cannot stand that the whole world is not studying *Chassidus*, because it is standing in his way. He wants to go outside, in Times Square, and the big billboards will have *Chassidus* on them. That, he says, is the real *pnimiyus chachma*: that he can't stand that the world is not studying *Chassidus*.

sections.title: The highest weeping: the Essence does not fit in the mind
sections.summary: There is a weeping above the first two: having understood the explanation, he sees that the thing itself can never fit in his mind. That total lack, felt in a way of a *yesh* of *bina*, weighs the same as the joy he would have if he grasped the Essence; it is the vessel for the secrets of the Torah, and it is the comprehension.

blocks.text: **Now, there is a weeping higher than this**, even higher: it comes from the absence of comprehension because of the greatness of the *hafla'a* and the separateness, **because the vessels of his mind cannot contain it**. And this is in *bina*, not in *chachma*. The first one was the weeping from the lack of understanding of the explanation. The second one was the *hafla'a*: he feels how far away it is from his seeing, and that is why he weeps. This one is the lack of understanding because of the thing itself, not because he didn't understand it yet.

The lack of understanding in *bina* awakens the second, the *hafla'a* of *chachma*; and the *hafla'a* of *chachma* awakens the third, which is now back to understanding: now he understands that this is totally gone from him, that the vessels of his mind cannot contain it. It is not understandable. Not that he didn't understand the explanation: he understood the explanation, fine, to the point that he had the total *hafla'a* from it. And now he sees that it is not a thing he is going to get by understanding the explanations. He understood the explanation, but he is not going to understand the actual thing, because it won't fit in his brain, no matter what he does.
