phrases.en: And this is in the wondrousness of the *Hidden of all hidden*,

phrases.he: דהיינו בעצמות אור אין סוף ממש
phrases.en: that is, in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* itself,

phrases.he: אשר בלתי מושג כלל
phrases.en: which is not grasped at all;

phrases.he: אדרבה, כל שיעמיק יותר, יותר יפלא כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: on the contrary, the deeper he goes, the more wondrous it is, as said above.

blocks.text: When Rabbi Akiva heard the deep secrets, his eyes ran with tears, because his brain couldn't take them in. This is **the wondrousness of the *Hidden of all hidden***, the Essence of the *Ein Sof* itself, totally not grasped: you can't understand it. Just the opposite: **the deeper he goes, the more wondrous it is**; the more you look into it, the farther away it is, as we explained before. And even more than that: as far as the *bina* goes, it is totally separate, even higher than for *chachma*, so that you have absolutely no *bina* into it at all. Zero. Absolute zero.

phrases.he: שמזה דוקא לבו דואג ובוכה.
phrases.en: From this precisely his heart worries and weeps;

phrases.he: שאינו בא רק מעוצם התענוג והתשוקה להשיג,
phrases.en: it comes only from the greatness of the delight and the longing to comprehend,

phrases.he: ואינו יכול כו'
phrases.en: and he cannot.

phrases.he: וידוע שזהו עיקר בחינת הכלי לבחינת חכמה ברזין דאורייתא
phrases.en: And it is known that this is the main vessel for *chachma* in the secrets of the Torah,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין אין מוסרין רזי תורה אלא למי שלבו דואג בקרבו כו'
phrases.en: as is written elsewhere on "the secrets of the Torah are given over only to one whose heart worries within him."

blocks.text: **From this precisely his heart worries and weeps**. Why? Remember the whole thing of *bina*: what does he want to understand? Why did he start learning *Chassidus*? He wants to understand G-d. So the weeping comes only from the greatness of the delight and the longing to comprehend, and he can't. It is exactly the opposite: the same as when his family went to the airport and left. The great loss he feels, and he's crying, is exactly how much pleasure he had when they were there.

**this is the main vessel for *chachma* in the secrets of the Torah**: a *chachma* which comes after the *bina*, by the way. It does not mean a *chachma* of *bittul*; it means actually knowing, like the Arizal, or like the Rebbe.

**as is written elsewhere** on "the secrets of the Torah are given over". So he says: how could you understand, if it is not possible to understand? *Mosrin*, they are given over: it is given to him. He can't understand it, but the *Aibershter* can give it to him, because the *Aibershter* is the *Aibershter*. And not only that: the *Aibershter* does understand it, in a way of an explanation. They are given only to one whose heart worries within him: how come he can't understand the *Aibershter*?

And all this, by the way, can only happen through *hisbonenus*. You can't say, "Oh, I want to understand the *Aibershter*; this is a lie, I'm just starting in *Chassidus*; well, you told me yourself that it won't explain it anyway." It is not like that. These are three levels that come one from the other.

phrases.he: אבל כשהיה משיג לעצמות אור אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: But if he were to comprehend the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* itself,

phrases.he: שם הוא ענין השמחה בעצמותו
phrases.en: there is the joy in His Essence.

blocks.text: **But if he were to comprehend the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* itself**... His heart worries within him and he is crying totally, because he has absolutely no comprehension, zero comprehension, of the *Aibershter*. But if he were to comprehend the Essence, the *atzmus umahus* of the *Aibershter*, **there is the joy in His Essence**. "What do you mean, if he would understand?" Since there can be a crying from the lack of it, that lack is the same thing as the joy. Like how much he misses the people, that's how much he enjoys the people.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שהוא גלוי העונג האלה״י הבא במורגש דווקא,
phrases.en: And though it is a revelation of the G-dly delight that comes precisely in a felt way,

phrases.he: אבל שרשו באמת בעצמות התענוג הנעלם,
phrases.en: its root, in truth, is in the Essence of the hidden delight,

phrases.he: שממנו יצא היפוכו שהוא הבכיה מהעדרו
phrases.en: from which came out its opposite, the weeping over its absence,

phrases.he: שהוא הפלאה והבדלה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: which is the wondrousness and separateness said above;

phrases.he: כי ב' קווין הללו שקולין גם כן בשווה ממש
phrases.en: for these two lines also weigh *mamash* the same;

phrases.he: דהיינו שלפי ערך כח עוצם וגודל התענוג שהיה מתענג בעצמות דוקא כשהיה משיגו ממש,
phrases.en: that is, according to the measure of the great power of the delight he would delight in the Essence precisely, if he really comprehended it,

phrases.he: כך ימצא כח היפוכו,
phrases.en: so will be the power of its opposite,

phrases.he: שהוא הבכיה העמוקה כשלא יכילו כלי מוחו להשיג כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.
phrases.en: the deep weeping when the vessels of his mind cannot comprehend, as said above; and this is enough for one who understands.

blocks.text: **a revelation of the G-dly delight that comes precisely in a felt way**: it is a joy, not a *bittul*. The joy of comprehension is a felt delight. There is a difference: a *bittul*, as he said, is a delight that is not felt; he doesn't feel that he's there, and even this he doesn't feel. But this he does feel. **its root, in truth, is in the Essence of the hidden delight**, from which comes out its opposite: it is the same thing, the weeping and the lack, over a thing that is totally non-understandable.

**for these two lines also weigh *mamash* the same**: it is exactly the same thing. As we understood that in the first, in *bina*, and in the *bittul* of *chachma*, they all weigh *mamash* the same, so here: the total lack of understanding, because it is not understandable, and the total weeping he gets from it, and the total happiness he would get if he would actually understand the *Aibershter* Himself, weigh *mamash* the same. It's exactly the same thing.

How much he would enjoy himself, how happy he would be, if he would actually comprehend Him, **so will be the power of its opposite**, the deep weeping when the vessels of his mind cannot comprehend. It's the same thing, as you understand in love: how much he misses the people, that's how much he'll enjoy the people. Somebody he doesn't enjoy he won't miss, and somebody he won't miss he won't enjoy. So the same here. And this is only activated by the *hafla'a* of *chachma*: *bina* activates *chachma*, and *chachma* activates *bina* again, but a higher *bina*. And now he is going to give you the order of the levels. It is not that you say, "Okay, well, I miss the *Aibershter*." No: it is the levels.

sections.title: The order of the levels, and why the not-understanding is the vessel
sections.summary: Joy from what is comprehended and weeping when it is hidden; above it the hidden delight of *chachma* and disgust with all life; above that the joy of "they will rejoice in You" and the weeping when the mind cannot hold it. The power of *bina* is the power of not understanding, like a bow drawn back: the empty glass is the vessel, and only learning makes the emptiness felt.

phrases.he: ונמצא סדר המדרגות בדבר והיפוכו כך הם,
phrases.en: So the order of the levels in a thing and its opposite is this:

phrases.he: חדוה ושמחה מגלוי אור אלה״י המושג ממש,
phrases.en: joy and gladness from the revelation of G-dly light that is actually comprehended,

phrases.he: והיפוכו יוצא בכיה בהסתר המנגד לזה
phrases.en: and its opposite comes out as weeping in the concealment that opposes it.

phrases.he: ולמעלה מזה בבחינת ענג וחדוה הנעלם שבכח מ''ה דחכמה בעצמות אלהו״ת המהווה כו',
phrases.en: Higher than this, in the hidden delight and joy in the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, in the Essence of the G-dliness that brings into being,

phrases.he: וכחו בהיפוכו יוצא למאוס בחייו ובחיי כל זולתו,
phrases.en: its power in its opposite comes out as disgust with his own life and the life of everything besides him,

phrases.he: כמו מי לי כו'
phrases.en: as in "Whom do I have..."

blocks.text: **So the order of the levels in a thing and its opposite is this**: it has to go up and down like this. **joy and gladness from the revelation of G-dly light that is actually comprehended**, which means in explanation; **and its opposite comes out as weeping**, when he doesn't understand the explanation quite well yet, because it is hard to understand.

**Higher than this**, the hidden delight and joy in the *koach MaH* of *chachma*; and its opposite comes out as **disgust with his own life and the life of everything besides him**. Not only his own life: he can't stand the whole world. He can't stand anybody doing anything but learning *Chassidus*. Nothing matters, and he doesn't care for nothing. He doesn't want to know from the angels, he doesn't want to know from nothing. If you tell him, "Well, why don't you calm down? We'll send you to heaven," he says, "I don't want to go to heaven."

phrases.he: ולמעלה גם מזה הענג והחדוה העצמיים בעצמות אלהו״ת דוקא,
phrases.en: And higher even than this, the essential delight and joy in the Essence of G-dliness itself,

phrases.he: כמו וישמחו בך ממש בגלוי כו'
phrases.en: as in "they will rejoice in You" *mamash*, revealed;

phrases.he: כוחו בהיפוכו יוצא כאשר לא יכילו כלי מוחו להכיל כו', יבכה
phrases.en: its power in its opposite comes out when the vessels of his mind cannot contain it: he will weep.

blocks.text: **And higher even than this**, the essential joy in the Essence itself: that's the joy, **as in "they will rejoice in You" *mamash*, revealed**. They will actually have joy in the Essence *mamash*, in a revealed way, and in a way that they can actually explain: in comprehension, with an explanation. "Where is the explanation?" Here it is: this book is explanation. And its opposite, the opposite of "they will rejoice in You" *mamash*, is when his brain cannot take it in: then **he will weep**.

phrases.he: (וכמו בכיה דאוהב הנאמן בנפשו בהפרדו,
phrases.en: (Like the weeping of a faithful, devoted friend when they part,

phrases.he: כדוד ויהונתן דאהבת נפשו אהבו,
phrases.en: as David and Yehonasan, "for he loved him as his own soul,"

phrases.he: דכתיב וישקו ויבכו כו'
phrases.en: as it is written, "they kissed and they wept,"

phrases.he: שבא מכח ריבוי אהבה בתענוג הגדול שביחודם ודבוקם כו' וכה"ג).
phrases.en: which comes from the abundance of love, in the great delight of their union and their attachment; and the like.)

blocks.text: **Like the weeping of a faithful, devoted friend when they part**, like we were saying before, at the airport: like David and Yehonasan, "**they kissed and they wept**". When they were separated, they cried. Why did they cry? Because of how happy they were to be together. It's exactly the same thing.

And that is precisely the *kli* for the comprehension. That is the *kli*. It is not just the *kli* for the comprehension: it is the comprehension. That is the whole thing we said about understanding: the power of understanding is that you don't understand. Unlike many other things, in understanding the whole power of understanding comes from not understanding.

How much you realize that you don't understand something, that's how much you'll get a power to do this *hisbonenus* and to understand. Like right now: why are we studying? Because we don't understand. And what are we doing? We are doing *hisbonenus*, and the *hisbonenus* is from not understanding. *Bina sheb'bina*, which means *pnimiyus bina*, the inner core of *bina*, is the power of not understanding. Exactly according to how much you think you don't understand, that's how strong the *bina* will be. A person who thinks he understands everything isn't going to: how much could there be already to understand by the *Aibershter*? What could there be to understand already? In general it's almost self-obvious that the power of *bina* is the power of not understanding. That's why you're learning.

blocks.title: Going to college to be a doctor
blocks.text: The whole *bina sheb'bina* means to learn. If I tell you, "I'm going to college," you say, "What are you learning there?" "I'm learning to be a doctor." That means I don't know yet how to be a doctor. That's why I'm learning. Learning means you're learning what you don't understand: that's the whole thing of learning.

So it is exactly according to how much he doesn't understand in G-dliness. When he learns *Chassidus*, first there will be the crying that he doesn't understand the explanation, because it's so hard to understand. Then, exactly according to how much he does understand, he will get a sense of how far: he'll see that it's far away. And that sense of how far will show him that it is not just hard to understand but impossible to understand; and not just impossible, it is not an understandable thing in the first place. That is the real power of *bina*, and that awakens the power of *bina*. Exactly according to how much he doesn't understand, that's how much he will understand.

blocks.title: The bow and the arrow
blocks.text: It goes by the negative power, like a bow and arrow: the more you pull the bow back, the farther the arrow will fly. So if he pulls it back to the total non-understanding, that there is absolutely zero understanding in *bina*, this will go directly into what the zero understanding is in: the Essence.

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: This is basically a *maamar* of the Frierdiker Rebbe, *Balayla hahu nadedah shnas hamelech*, "That night the king's sleep was disturbed". When you say that verse in the Megillah, you're supposed to say it louder. Why? Because that was the essence of the whole miracle: that Achashverosh couldn't sleep. So he asks: what does it mean? What about what happened before? Vashti died; wasn't the main miracle when Esther became the queen? He explains in terms of *Chassidus*: "that night" is the exile, and "the king", wherever it says "the king" in the Megillah, is the King of the world.

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: The exile is called *dormita d'Zeir Anpin*, the sleep of *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance; *dormita* is from *dormir*, to sleep). When *Zeir Anpin* is sleeping, everything is on one level. When a person is up, the head is above and the feet are below. When a person is sleeping, everything is on the same level: the feet think they're on the same level as the head, because they are. And the *middos* are all mixed up: the brain does not control *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*, or *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*. It could even be the opposite, and that is the whole matter of dreams: the dreams come from the liver, from *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*. There are three vessels, brain, heart and liver. When you stand up, the brain is the highest, the heart next, and the liver the lowest. When you're sleeping it's all on the same level, and the liver can make up a whole bunch of dreams. So this is very nice. And the king woke up.

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: And in the future the redemption will come, *Moshiach*, and then the King will really wake up; because there, His sleep was only disturbed, and then He went back to sleep. He just got woken up for a little bit. But he says: "That's all very nice. It's a very nice Kabbalistic explanation. But why does He have to sleep in the first place?" Why is He sleeping? First of all it says, "Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps," and then it says, "Awake, why do You sleep?": wake up, *Aibershter*, why are You sleeping? So why is He sleeping? He explains that the whole exile is like a dream, the dream of *Zeir Anpin*, and in a dream all kinds of crazy things can happen.

blocks.title: An elephant through the eye of a needle
blocks.text: You can open your door and walk out the door, and you're in China. A tree can grow upside down: a tree growing from the ceiling, going down. All kinds of crazy things. But in *Shaar HaYichud* (the Gate of Unity), towards the end of the book where he explains where the dreams come from, he says that the demons come and mix up the letters from the daytime: you dream at night only what you think in the day; the demons mix it up, a letter from this word and a letter from that word. And he says: but an elephant through the eye of a needle you won't dream. It is only things like in the daytime; something totally ridiculous, like an elephant through the eye of a needle, you don't dream. The Frierdiker Rebbe brings a quote from someplace: an elephant through the eye of a needle, where could that happen? Only in a dream. "What are you talking about? Didn't the Mitteler Rebbe say you don't dream an elephant through the eye of a needle?" He says, "Yes: that's where the dream is from the thoughts of the heart in the daytime. That's a normal dream."

blocks.title: An elephant through the eye of a needle
blocks.text: But then there are nightmares, where the dream gets totally crazy and is nothing like the daytime anymore. In a terrible nightmare you finally realize that you're in a nightmare; in a regular dream you don't realize you're dreaming. It's so terrible that the person wakes himself up, because he can't take it anymore: it's so crazy that he realizes it's a dream. In a dream like that, he says, an elephant can go into the eye of a needle. Only in a dream: in a nightmare. "And that's why the *Aibershter* went to sleep."

Why? Because He wanted to have a nightmare, so we should end up in Europe, and then in America finally. And what can happen in a nightmare? The biggest thing: an elephant can go into the eye of a needle. The elephant, *pila*, is the biggest animal, and the eye of a needle, *kufa d'machta*, is the littlest thing; and the roots of the words are *pila*, *pele*, wonder, and *machta*, *chotei*, a sinner. That means that the *Aibershter* can go into the brain of not even Rabbi Akiva, but a normal sinner, a *rasha*, a total American *shvantz*. And where can that happen? There was a book, "Only in America". That's the whole reason for the exile: for the elephant in the eye of the needle. What's the elephant in the eye of the needle? This thing here that can't fit in his brain; it's not possible to fit it in his brain. But in America you can do anything. Everything is possible in America. They told the Frierdiker Rebbe, "This is America."

blocks.text: (He has to stop here.) So that is the *kli*. The *kli* for the actual comprehension of the Essence is the total lack of comprehension. But the total lack of comprehension should be a felt thing, in a way of a *yesh* of *bina*; not even in the way of the *ayin* of the *hafla'a* of *chachma*, but in the way of a *yesh* of *bina*. To do that, you have to learn *Chassidus* first. Everybody says, "Oh well, I don't understand, and I also don't understand nothing in G-dliness; so does that mean that I should understand G-dliness?" No. By you it is just a hidden thing that you don't understand G-dliness: you have no idea that you *mamash* understand zero, absolutely zero, that you have absolutely no comprehension. When you learn *Chassidus*, it is by way of comprehension: you have nothing, you don't understand anything.

That is what it means when he says that the vessel of the mind cannot contain it. Even when you say an elephant through the eye of a needle, there is still a sort of proportion. Really it is not even like that: the vessel has absolutely no room at all to take this thing in, and this thing is absolutely too big to go into anything. And you have to have an actual feeling of this, in the way of a *yesh*: you should actually feel how much this thing is lacking in understanding, in the way of comprehension. And that is the *kli*.

blocks.title: A glass is its emptiness
blocks.text: You know what a *kli* is? A *kli* is a vacuum. The main thing of the glass is the emptiness: not the body of the glass, but its empty part. If you have a full *kli*, you can't put nothing into it. That's the thing: everybody has a full *kli*. If you have the proper *bina*, the real thing of *bina* is that it is totally devoid of G-dliness, totally. It is the best *kli* for G-dliness because it is totally empty of G-dliness. That's why a vacuum sucks: a vacuum wants to be filled. And not only that: the whole matter of *bina* is that it wants to be filled with G-dliness.

That is the main matter of *bina*: it wants to know the true nature of reality. You say that's not really *bina* into G-dliness: how come people are doing *bina* into all kinds of other things? Look at the scientist: what is he doing it for? He wants to know the true nature of reality. That's the whole thing of *bina*. They don't want to know just to know things. The real thing of *bina*, of a guy who is a *mevin*, the intellectual, is that he wants to know the true nature of reality; he doesn't want to know just some stupid thing. So that's the best *kli*.

sections.title: The answer: the joy reaches the Essence, now through weeping and in the future as laughter
sections.summary: *Bina*, most opposed to the Essence, gets closest: it gives an approximation that *chachma* fills in, and the grasp is real. So the comprehension is of a *tzimtzum* while the joy is in the Essence itself; now it comes out through the weeping of exile, and in the future, eye to eye, as laughter.

phrases.he: ובכ"ז מתורץ ענין הנזכר לעיל בשמחה שבבינה וענג שבחכמה,
phrases.en: With all this, what was said above about the joy in *bina* and the delight in *chachma* is answered:

phrases.he: דגם שההשגה עצמה היא בבחינת צמצום אור האלה״י שמשיגו,
phrases.en: though the comprehension itself is of a *tzimtzum* of the G-dly light that he comprehends,

phrases.he: אבל השמחה שרשה מגיע בעצמות אלהו״ת דוקא
phrases.en: the joy has its root reaching the Essence of G-dliness itself;

blocks.text: To go over it a little: of all the *sefiros*, *bina* is the one that has the most opposition, so it is the one that can get the closest. The biggest weeping is not in *chachma* but really in *bina*. The first weeping, of *bina*, is not as big as the second weeping, of *chachma*; but that wakes up the third weeping, of *bina*: not that he didn't understand it yet, that he didn't have the explanation yet, but that even now that he has the explanation, he sees that the explanation is not into the actual Essence.

blocks.text: So the longing for the *Aibershter* is strongest precisely in *bina*, because in all the other things you get a certain amount of satisfaction. You know the Rolling Stones song, "I can't get no satisfaction"? That is strongest precisely in *bina*, because *bina* can never get any satisfaction at all. In love or fear you do get a certain amount of love and fear; and in *chachma*, the *hafla'a* is precisely from the Essence. The love and the fear are of the Essence too: you don't get an actual grasp of the Essence (that is in *bina*, that you don't get the grasp), but the love is for the Essence, and the same with the fear, the *hafla'a*, *daas*, the upper *Keser*, the *ratzon* and the *taanug*: they are for the Essence. But in *bina*, as was said, if you understand it, it is not the Essence.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: Not only that: *bina* is basically like this perfect vacuum cleaner, where the more you put into it, the emptier it gets. All the other ones get a certain amount put into them. One of the things about the *sefiros* is that there are ten kinds of *avodos* (services): an *avoda* from each *sefira*, the same as there are ten kinds of people, ten general types. Really each person is a mixture, like different characters are a mixture. Down here there is no such thing as a person who is all *chesed* or all *gevura*; but some people lean more to *chesed*, some more to *gevura*, some more to emotions, some more to brains.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And the same in *avoda*. There is no special *avoda* that is only love, because without *hisbonenus*, we say, there is no love. So there are two things. First, all the *avodos* depend on *bina*: that is what he said in chapter one, and that is the whole matter of *Kuntres HaHispaalus* (the Tract on Ecstasy), that if there is no *hisbonenus* there is no *avoda*. The *avoda* of *Malchus* is accepting the yoke of the kingship of Heaven; there is an *avoda* of love and fear; *netzach* is the *avoda* of overcoming (there are various matters in it, but the one you usually think of is overcoming your bad habits by willpower); and *hoda'a* means to be *modeh*, to acknowledge. Even *hoda'a* needs a certain amount of *bina*: *hoda'a* means that you acknowledge more than you understand. That's why *hod* comes out of *bina*, as it says in chapter thirty-three.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: (The line has an echo.) Besides that all the other *avodos* actually depend on *bina*, the other thing is that in all the other *avodos* there is a sense of satisfaction. It is like when you eat: the more you eat, the less hungry you get. In *bina* it's not like that; it's the opposite. In *bina*, the more you feed it, the hungrier it gets. It is not like eating, where the more you eat, the more you get a certain sense of satisfaction and a certain sense of pleasure. Here you get just the opposite: even though you get joy, the *taanug* actually gets farther away.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And not only that: the *hafla'a* of *chachma* comes precisely from the *bina*, as he said in these last two chapters. Love and fear too come precisely from the *hisbonenus*, as it says in many places. As a matter of fact it is a *halacha* according to the *Rambam*: he explains that to get the love and fear it comes precisely like that, and that is how he starts his whole *Yad HaChazaka*. And even accepting the yoke of the kingship of Heaven, which means that you accept the yoke without intellect, still needs a certain amount of *bina* to get started.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: Like the song we were talking about yesterday, the Rebbe's song, one of the songs the Rebbe *mamash* sang himself. The words say, "My soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You": the thirst is both spiritual and physical. And how is it? "In a dry and weary land, without water": no water at all. No water at all is precisely in *bina*; everywhere else it is not a pure vacuum, there is some water. And then it continues, "*Kein* in holiness I have beheld You". *Kein* here does not mean yes; it means thus: through this having no water at all, I see You in the holiness. And then it says, "to see Your strength and Your glory". To see is precisely a thing of *chachma*. But a *chizayon*, a beholding, does not mean actually to see. It is like a stargazer: a *chizayon* is actually an approximation, not a clear sight; a vision, or something like that.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.question: You say bina is the opposite of the Essence and that is why it can grasp the Essence; but if you grasp it, it is not the Essence. So how can you say it does grasp the Essence?
blocks.text: What *bina* actually is, is an approximation, or a simulation, like a *chizayon*. A *chizayon* is like the way you get a picture on a computer screen.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's picture on the computer screen
blocks.text: When he turns on his computer, the background picture is a picture of the Rebbe, or any picture. If you magnify that picture, you'll see that it's made out of pixels: a bunch of dots. Make it bigger and bigger, and you'll finally see that it's not really a picture of the Rebbe at all. It's really just a bunch of details, and that's the whole matter of *bina*: it supplies details. And there is a thing, he doesn't remember what they call it in computer language, the level of clarity: 320 by 400, 600 by 800, 1200 by 1500, more and more levels of clarity. Also, certain pages, when you're downloading them, don't fill in from the top down. They start filling all over, and you get something that looks like a bunch of squares, and you can't see what it is yet. ("You're not such a big computer freak like me and Shimon.")
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's picture on the computer screen
blocks.text: As it fills in, you fill in some details, and some more details, and you still can't see what it is, but you can see that it's a human face. You can't tell yet exactly who it is, because it's all a bunch of squares; it's not filled in properly. As it fills in more and more, finally you can see it, and finally you *mamash* see the Rebbe's face, just like the Rebbe is standing in front of you. But really it is still just an approximation, the same as before, when you couldn't see. Before it was like 20 by 40, then it filled in more and more, to 200 by 300; his computer is a slightly older one, 640 by 800 or something like that, and some of the newer ones are 1200 by 1500, so it looks really sharp. But really he can see the Rebbe. It doesn't look to him like a bunch of pixels at all. It looks just like when he stood in front of the Rebbe.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Your eyes are made of pixels
blocks.text: And if you think about it a little bit: right now you're looking around and seeing the room, right? It's not true. It's pixels. Your eyes are made of pixels. The back of the eye, the retina, is made up of these pixels of different colors, which work exactly the same way as a TV, except that they are receptors. There are pixels of different colors which receive, and that's why, if you look at the sun or a bright light and then look away, you still have an afterimage: they get slightly burnt out until they regenerate themselves.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: A movie is still pictures
blocks.text: So even when you are seeing anything, what you're really seeing is an approximation. It's the same thing as in a movie. In a movie you're not really seeing anybody moving; nobody is moving at all. It's a bunch of still pictures: the details. ("It's an optical illusion.") Well, it's not just an optical illusion; it's a little bit more than that. Like when you see the Rebbe's face on the screen: it looks like an optical illusion really, but it's not just an optical illusion.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Close enough for folk music
blocks.text: What happens is that the *chachma* fills in the spaces of the *bina*. On a computer screen, when you see a circle, it's not really a circle. It's really a multi-gon: there's a hexagon and an octagon and a decagon ("there are thousands of little edges"); it depends how many edges there are. Octagon means eight edges. On a 640 by 800 screen it's not a real circle, because a real circle has infinite edges, and on 640 by 800 you can't get infinite edges. But it's like what they say: close enough for folk music. It doesn't matter, because by the time it gets translated by your *chachma*, the *chachma* fills in the extra edges, and you see a circle. And this is what it says: the *bina* and the *chachma* work together.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: This is the same thing. Notice the way he started off: a lot of times you wonder why he starts off a chapter a certain way, and then he jumps and says, "Oh, but first we have to do something else." In chapter five, before he jumped into the rest of chapter five and chapter six, he says you have to know all the particular divisions of levels in all the particulars of the chain of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and they will all be explained in a special tract. He's going to explain everything, all the points. But then he says: wait a minute, you can't explain all the points. "What is needed from every *prat*": I'm going to tell you what you need from every particular, "and automatically the one who understands will understand and know several other particulars". In other words: I will give you the approximation, and automatically you'll fill in the rest of the particulars. You'll see a circle. I'll give you enough points, as many as you need. And that is the thing of *bina*: to give you the points, to give you the particulars.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And if you notice, later on in the book, where he explains the matters of *chachma* and *bina*, he says that the *chachma* is automatic, *mimeila*: the *chachma* comes on its own. You don't have to make an effort to make it a circle, or to see the movie as a moving picture. It is automatic. That is also what he explains later about joining to *chachma*: the *bina* cuts up the idea, it dissects the idea into more and more until it finally has it in letters. It cuts it down into concepts, the concepts into smaller concepts, into words, all the way into letters; and then it takes the letters and transfers them over one at a time: the mother lends the clothing to the daughter, speech.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Bah, boo: no word is ever said
blocks.text: Like what's happening now: he is really talking one letter at a time. If you make a time study, you'll see that at no point did he say an actual word. A word takes several points of time. And if you look at the book, you'll see that there is not a single word in it: there's a bunch of letters, and there's spaces. But when you listen to him, or look at the book, your *chachma* puts it together automatically. You don't have to make an effort: "Wait a minute, he said ah, and then he said ooh, and then he said bah, and then he said boo, so that means something." You don't have to think like that: "Oh, wait a minute, what word did he say? If bah and boo, what does that mean? Bah-boo? Oh, okay." It happens automatically, and that's what he says here: *mimeila*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: So the basic thing is, as it says, "thus in holiness I have beheld You": I have the *chizayon* of You, and from this I get the *chachma* of Your strength and Your glory, which is already not really You. It's the strength of You and the glory of You. The *chachma* is not really into the You: the *chachma* is actually into the Name, into the light. "What do you mean? The *bina* never at any point gets the actual self." He says, "Yes, so what? It gives you better and better approximations." "Okay, but that's still not the actual self."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The voice on the telephone
blocks.text: The picture of the Rebbe is not the actual Rebbe. But right now, what's happening is that his voice is being turned into approximations, electric pulses, and what you're getting over there is not really exactly his voice. ("Well, it's not even your voice at all, really.") Yes, but even the thing you're getting there is not exactly how he talked over here; it's an approximation. ("Of course.") Okay, but it makes no difference. You're talking to him, and he's talking to you. The grasp that you get is actual: it makes no difference that it's an approximation. That's the whole thing. And so it is precisely *bina* that catches the *etzem*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And that's also why, as it says in various places, *bina* is *teshuva ila'a* (the higher return). Why would *bina* be *teshuva ila'a*? You'd think *teshuva ila'a* is a guy crying, some kind of an emotion. Why *bina*? Because it says, "The soul returns to *Havaya*", or was it "to G-d"; he can't remember what it says. The matter of *teshuva* is that you have to return all the way to G-d. Not part of the way: all the way. And this is only possible with *bina*, because all the other ones are not 100%.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And also, there are two matters in *teshuva*. One is to return all the way to the *Aibershter*. The other, which is the main thing in *teshuva*, is to realize how far away you are from the *Aibershter*. And this is precisely by *bina*. Only in *bina* does he really realize that he has absolutely nothing to do with the *Aibershter* at all. Nothing, totally nothing: all the understandings and all the emotions and everything are totally nothing, and have nothing to do with it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: (They find the place, a little more than the middle of the page, 226.) So he says that the order of the levels is *bina*: the weeping of *bina*, because he doesn't understand the explanation yet; then the weeping of *chachma*, because of the sense of *hafla'a*, how far it is; and finally the weeping of *bina*, because he sees that it is totally not understandable. **With all this, what was said above about the joy in *bina* and the delight in *chachma* is answered**: **though the comprehension itself is of a *tzimtzum* of the G-dly light**, not of the actual G-dliness, and not even of the actual light, but of the *tzimtzum* of the light, **the joy has its root reaching the Essence of G-dliness itself**.

phrases.he: כמו הנשמות נהנין מזיו השכינה ממש בגן עדן
phrases.en: as the souls *mamash* enjoy the radiance of the *Shechina* in *Gan Eden*,

phrases.he: גם השגתם באה על ידי צמצום כידוע
phrases.en: though their comprehension too comes through a *tzimtzum*, as is known.

phrases.he: וזהו וישמחו בך דוקא,
phrases.en: And this is "they will rejoice in You," precisely;

phrases.he: והיינו חדווא בסטרא דא ובכיה היפוכה יוצא מכחה בג' מיני מדריגות הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that is, joy on one side, and weeping, its opposite, coming out of its power, in the three kinds of levels said above;

phrases.he: וב' קווין שקולין הם בשווה ממש כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and the two lines weigh *mamash* the same, as said above.

blocks.text: **as the souls *mamash* enjoy the radiance of the *Shechina* in *Gan Eden***, **though their comprehension too comes through a *tzimtzum***. And that is what **"they will rejoice in You," precisely** means: actually in the Essence. Joy on one side, and weeping, its opposite, coming out of it, in the three levels; and these two lines are exactly the two sides of the same thing, *mamash* equal.

phrases.he: וזהו בשמחה ובטוב לבב מרוב כל,
phrases.en: And this is "with joy and gladness of heart, from the abundance of everything,"

phrases.he: בהשגת המהוה
phrases.en: in the comprehension of the One who brings into being.

blocks.text: **"with joy and gladness of heart, from the abundance of everything,"**: you will serve the *Aibershter* with joy and gladness of heart from having so much of everything, **in the comprehension of the One who brings into being**: an actual comprehension, not of what is brought into being, but of the One who brings it into being. The comprehension starts off being only into what is brought into being; but finally you'll have the joy and gladness of heart from the abundance of everything. You'll have everything, the whole thing: the comprehension of the One who brings into being, actually.

phrases.he: וכמו לעתיד דכתיב עין בעין נראה כו'
phrases.en: As in the future, of which it is written, "Eye to eye we will see,"

phrases.he: ואמר ביום ההוא הנה אלהינ״ו זה,
phrases.en: and it says, "On that day: Behold, this is our G-d,"

phrases.he: לנוכח,
phrases.en: face to face;

phrases.he: אז נגילה ונשמחה בו דווקא כידוע ודי למבין
phrases.en: then "we will exult and rejoice in Him," precisely, as is known; and this is enough for one who understands.

phrases.he: אבל עכשיו כל זה בוקע ויוצא על ידי המנגד,
phrases.en: But now all this breaks through and comes out by way of the opposite,

phrases.he: היפוכו דוקא, שהוא הבכיה מסטרא דא
phrases.en: its opposite precisely, which is the weeping on one side,

phrases.he: עד רום המעלות וכמו שכתוב בבכי יבואו דוקא,
phrases.en: up to the highest of levels; as it is written, "With weeping they will come," precisely,

phrases.he: וכן הלוך ילך ובכה כו'
phrases.en: and "He goes along weeping."

blocks.text: **As in the future**, it is written, "Eye to eye": you'll *mamash* see the *Aibershter* eye to eye. **"On that day: Behold, this is our G-d,"** right in front of us: *this* is this. Not *koh*, "like this": this is the *Aibershter*. We'll be able to say the exact thing, **face to face**, right in front of us. **then "we will exult and rejoice in Him," precisely**, when *Moshiach* comes; it is plain. **But now** it is precisely through the opposite, the weeping of the exile, on one side, up to the highest levels, as it says, **"With weeping they will come," precisely**, and "**He goes along weeping**".

This is also the whole matter of the exile and the redemption. ("Just one minute.") What he is saying here is that even though the comprehension itself is of a *tzimtzum* of G-dly light, so that you don't really understand it, what you rejoice in is the Essence. "Yes, but it's more than that. It says that finally the comprehension will be in the Essence." Finally the comprehension will be in the Essence, because it is a *mashal* on a *mashal*, "and to understand one thing from another": from the externality of the One who brings into being he will understand, he will actually have the comprehension of the One who brings into being, not of what is brought into being. In other words, he will climb up the levels in *bina*.

That's first of all. First of all, the joy of *bina*, the joy that we are getting, is not from understanding psychological concepts. The joy is in G-d Himself. Even right now, according to these contracted comprehensions, the joy is still in the "in Him". It makes no difference. That's the whole joy that we're getting. We're not getting a joy because right now we're talking about the psychology of understanding, how the human mind works. That's not where we're getting the joy from. We're not interested in that at all, actually.

The joy that we're getting is because we are slowly getting filled in the *chizayon* of G-dliness. We fill in one little detail, another little detail, and slowly we start to actually see a picture. Even when we're talking about a detail, the joy we get is because of the G-dliness in it: we're getting the joy from the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for), not from the *mashal*. Like when you say, "Oh, the light of the sun: there's this fantastic explosion." So who cares? That's not what we're getting the joy from.

And the thing with the exile and the redemption: what did the *Aibershter* see to pick precisely idiots like us, especially since *bina* is from the highest things? He picked guys who really, according to the levels of how they used to be, don't really have no *middos*, and don't have much of a *sechel* (intellect) either. Why? First of all, because we don't have no *middos* to interfere with the *bina*, so we can't get any sense of accomplishment or enjoyment from anywhere else, only from the *bina*. And in the *bina*, the more he doesn't understand, the more he is connected to G-dliness.

We don't understand better than any of the previous generations. ("Yeah, we're pretty good at not understanding.") We're total idiots. Not just us: the whole generation. You'd think, why didn't He pick the older generations, who could have understood this better? It is precisely because of that: because the sense of not understanding is the strongest by us, and we're the farthest away. So this is basically the matter of *teshuva ila'a*, and the whole matter of the *yichudim* (unifications), and everything: everything is precisely from *bina*. *Bina* is the central... (the side ends here).

As he said, this particular chapter is really a fantastic chapter in terms of pulling together the whole beginning of the book: of the different *avodos* it is precisely *bina*, for two reasons. One: even if you are going to choose another *avoda*, that *avoda* also depends on *bina*. The *avoda* of love and fear, for instance, is really also *hisbonenus*, because it is the *bina* that awakens all the other faculties. So no matter which way you look at it, it is really the main *avoda*. Even if you want an *avoda* of love and fear, it has to be through the *bina*: you can't have love and fear without the *bina*. And even an *avoda* of *hafla'a* is only through the *bina*. So the main *avoda*, even of the other nine *avodos*, is *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 070 opens with this, before it rereads lines 58-60.

blocks.text: But then there is the *avoda* of *bina* itself. The other ones are called, in a way, *avodas halev* (the service of the heart), and even *avodas halev* is really *bina*. But in *avodas hamochin* it is pure *bina*, unconnected with the emotions altogether. And even the highest *avoda*, *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d), is really precisely *bina*. It is not an *avoda* of *daas*. It is called *daas Havaya* because that is the result. The result is *daas*: like what he told them, that he couldn't sleep because his mind was all fired up with this thing and he couldn't remove the focus from it. That's the result. But the actual *avoda* is *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 070 opens with this, before it rereads lines 58-60.

blocks.text: And the whole matter of grasping the knowledge of the Essence is exactly the opposite of what people say. People think, "After all, the Essence is totally non-understandable." ("That's right.") The Essence is totally non-understandable: not just because it's so hard to understand, it's beyond understanding. But the conclusion they draw from it is the main point of the breaking of the vessels. The main point of the breaking is in *bina*, SaG of SaG; you notice that *bina* is also the source of the *kelipos*, the source of the breaking and the source of the repair: the eighth king of *Tohu*. The conclusion they drew is: since *bina* is not into the Essence at all, you should stay away from *bina* and go to *daas*. Instead of eating from the Tree of Life, he ate from the Tree of Knowledge. And it is exactly the upside-down conclusion: they don't get it, it's basically shoe on head. That *bina*, more than any other *sefira*, is not into the Essence is what makes it have the most to do with the Essence. It sucks the Essence into it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 070 opens with this, before it rereads lines 58-60.

phrases.he: ולעתיד לבא יהיה השחוק
phrases.en: And in the time to come there will be laughter,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אז ימלא שחוק פינו
phrases.en: as it is written, "Then our mouth will be filled with laughter,"

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין הקניגיא כו'
phrases.en: and as is written elsewhere on the *kenigya* (the joust);

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב כי אתה אבינו, זה יצחק,
phrases.en: and this is "For you are our father": this is Yitzchak,

phrases.he: שצחוק זה בא לעתיד מן המנגד שלו, אשר בחינת הבכיה היה בגלות כידוע.

blocks.text: **And in the time to come there will be laughter**, as it says, **"Then our mouth will be filled with laughter,"** and the laughter is precisely from the Essence. And as it says elsewhere about the fight between the wild ox and the Leviathan: that's what **the *kenigya*** is. A *kenigya* means a joust, like the knights had: everybody sits and watches a fight. It says that the *Aibershter* will amuse the *tzaddikim* (the righteous) with the joust between the wild ox and the Leviathan. **"For you are our father": this is Yitzchak**: in the future we will say to Yitzchak that he is our father. Yitzchak is the master of the future, and from the weeping of the exile will come the laughter of the coming of *Moshiach*.

sections.title: Tikkun chatzos: the simple tear over the sins of youth prepares the way
sections.summary: The plain tears of the midnight lament over the sins of youth repair the source of the flaw, the casting off of the yoke, and become bread for prayer; they are the first step and the preparation for the three levels of weeping, the work the *shluchim* do in the world today.

phrases.he: ובכל זה יובן טעם האמיתי לענין תיקון חצות בבכיה דוקא
phrases.en: With all this, the true reason for *tikkun chatzos* (the midnight lament), with weeping precisely, will be understood:

phrases.he: שהוא תועלת לנפש להיות בתפילה גילוי תענוג העצמי, כמו וישמחו בך וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: it is a benefit for the soul, so that in prayer there will be a revelation of the essential delight, as in "they will rejoice in You," and the like.

phrases.he: והגם שהבכיה בתיקון חצות הוא דמעות פשוטים על חטאות נעורים וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: And though the weeping in *tikkun chatzos* is simple tears over the sins of youth and the like,

phrases.he: אבל על זה אמר היתה לי דמעתי לחם יומם ולילה
phrases.en: of this it says, "My tears have been my bread day and night,"

blocks.text: **the true reason for *tikkun chatzos*** (the midnight lament), with weeping precisely: it benefits the soul, so that in prayer there is a revelation of the essential delight, as in "they will rejoice in You". **simple tears over the sins of youth**, the *chatos ne'urim*. And this, by the way: these two chapters, not so much what they say about *bina* but about the weeping and the joy, the tears and the sins of youth, are expanded into a whole book, basically, in *Derech Chaim*.

blocks.title: The plane from Los Angeles to New York
blocks.text: **and the like**: the simple tears over the sins of youth are *mamash* the same thing as going towards the Essence. He explains the reason like this. You get on the plane from Los Angeles to New York, 3,000 miles, and the guy on the plane says, "We left Los Angeles, and we've gone 1,000 miles away from Los Angeles." So you ask him, "And how much closer to New York are we than when we left?" So he tells you, "Idiot, I told you, we're 1,000 miles farther from Los Angeles. So we have to be 1,000 miles closer to New York." It can't be any other way. If you're traveling along a certain line, how far you left from where you're leaving is how close you got to where you're going.

So the same thing: how far you went away from the sins of youth, that's how close you're getting to the *Aibershter*, *mamash* the same thing. So even though the weeping is simple tears, just a plain crying over his sins of youth and the like, of this it says, **"My tears have been my bread day and night,"**

blocks.text: **in the *Shema* and the prayer of the morning and the evening**: the tear of *tikkun chatzos* will be the bread of "day and night", of the *Shema* of the evening and the morning prayers. Day is *Shacharis*, and night is *Maariv*. Why?

**because the tears over his distance, which came from his iniquities and sins, repair the source of the flaw**, which is precisely the *perikas ol*, the casting off of the yoke of the kingship of Heaven. This is all covered in *Derech Chaim*, at very great length, and *Shaarei Orah* too talks about how the tear repairs the source of the flaw. Because the crying over the sins is actually about the reason for the sin, which is the casting off of the yoke. **and the exile of the *Shechina* comes in a particular way into every G-dly spark**: the general exile of the *Shechina* comes in a particular way into each G-dly spark. There is a spark of the *Shechina* in exile there.

phrases.en: And this tear will repair and remove the flaw completely,

phrases.en: and comes from the power of its opposite, which is the essential joy said above,

phrases.he: להיות ממש כמו לחם לנפשו כו'

blocks.text: **And this tear** comes from its opposite, the essential joy, **to shine in his G-dly soul in the *Shema* and prayer**. And notice that now he is talking about *teshuva tata'a* (the lower return), of *Malchus*. Before he was talking about *teshuva ila'a*. What he is telling you is that even *teshuva tata'a*, just simply crying about the sins, can bring him to G-dliness; but it is nothing like *teshuva ila'a*. **to be *mamash* like bread for his soul**: this crying over leaving the sins becomes *mamash* like actual food for his soul.

phrases.he: ולהיפוך בפריקות עול,
phrases.en: And the reverse, in casting off the yoke,

phrases.he: היפך הדמעה, כמו והתברך בלבבו
phrases.en: the opposite of the tear: as in "he blesses himself in his heart,

phrases.he: בשרירות לבי אלך כו'
phrases.en: I will go in the stubbornness of my heart";

phrases.he: כעבד שמורד,
phrases.en: like a servant who rebels,

phrases.he: שהמרידה ופריקות עול עיקר ומקור לכל שיעשה נגד רצון האדון כו':
phrases.en: for the rebellion and the casting off of the yoke are the main thing and the source of everything he will do against his master's will.

blocks.text: **And the reverse, in casting off the yoke**, which is the opposite of crying. A guy who casts off the yoke, what does it say? "**he blesses himself in his heart**": he thinks he's blessed. He says, "Eh, nothing could happen to me. **I will go in the stubbornness of my heart**: I'll do whatever I feel like." And he walks around like a big shot. **like a servant who rebels**: when a servant rebels and he's succeeding, or seemingly succeeding, he's strutting around.

But still, *bina* is *teshuva ila'a*, which totally includes this inside it. Especially in our days, a person doesn't even understand that he has a casting off of the yoke, and doesn't even understand how he can have one. If he understood that the master is really standing right there... And why doesn't he understand that? Because he doesn't have *hisbonenus*. So he doesn't know that he doesn't know. That's why he blesses himself: he thinks he's safe. He says, "I'm safe. I got away, and I can do whatever I want now."

phrases.he: והנה על זה אמר אוילים מדרך פשעם.
phrases.en: And of this it says, "Fools, because of the way of their transgression."

phrases.he: פשעים אלו המרדים בפריקת עול,
phrases.en: These transgressions are the rebellions of casting off the yoke;

phrases.he: גם שיתענו מעונותיהם בחטאות נעורים,
phrases.en: though they fast for their iniquities, for the sins of youth,

phrases.he: מה יועיל,
phrases.en: what will it help,

phrases.he: כי כל אוכל דחכמה הנזכר לעיל תתעב נפשם
phrases.en: for "their soul abhors all food," the food of wisdom said above,

phrases.he: היפך הענג שחיה תחיה לנפשו כו'
phrases.en: the opposite of the delight that gives life to his soul.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב ויגיעו עד שערי מות
phrases.en: And this is "They reached the gates of death,"

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב החיים והטוב,
phrases.en: as it is written, "life and the good,"

phrases.en: which is joy and goodness of heart in the essential delight said above,

phrases.he: והיפוכו מות ורע בפריקת עול

blocks.text: **"Fools, because of the way of their transgression."** The fools will leave the way of their transgression. **These transgressions are the rebellions of casting off the yoke**. A *pesha*, a transgression: he doesn't know how you say *pesha* in English ("a *poshei'a*"). Whatever: a *pesha* means not just something that's done, but done in a way of a *mered*, a rebellion, with a casting off of the yoke, that he's taken off the yoke. **though they fast for their iniquities, for the sins of youth** (this, by the way, is explained at great length in *Derech Chaim*), and they think they're leaving the sins of youth, **what will it help**? Why? Because "their soul abhors all food" of *chachma*: they don't want to learn *Chassidus*. So what's it going to help them to beat their chest?

**the opposite of the delight that gives life to his soul**: because the crying really comes from understanding what he did, and the crying is the opposite of the delight, which will enliven his soul. **"They reached the gates of death,"**: they will come up to the gates of death; as it says, "**life and the good**", which is joy and goodness of heart in the essential delight, **and its opposite is death and evil, in casting off the yoke**.

phrases.he: והדמעה בתיקון חצות דווקא הוא עיקר ההכנה בנפשו
phrases.en: And the tear in *tikkun chatzos* precisely is the main preparation in his soul

phrases.he: להיות בתפלה כל ענין הנזכר לעיל בג' מדריגות דבכיה מסטרא דא כו'
phrases.en: for there to be in his prayer all the above, in the three levels of weeping on one side...

blocks.text: **the main preparation in his soul** for the three levels. The crying in *tikkun chatzos* is basically the crying over the exile. And the real crying over the exile is not that, as in the ruling of the *Rambam*, they want *Moshiach* to come for all the goodies: that is not a real crying over the exile, not the crying of *tikkun chatzos*. The real crying is over being far away from the *Aibershter*: that he cast off the yoke, and so now he doesn't have the room to study properly. **the three levels of weeping**: this is the preparation for the whole matter later on of the three levels. In other words, this crying of *teshuva* is just a beginning: it is the *teshuva tata'a*.

But none of this part applies nowadays. It doesn't apply because we're doing *lechatchila ariber*. But even with the Rebbe, even when you're going *lechatchila ariber*, you have to know what you're jumping over: this is what you're jumping over. There is a matter of *teshuva tata'a*, of leaving the sins, and that does apply. It's not that it doesn't apply; it really does. It's just that it's done without weeping.

blocks.question: But even according to the Rebbe, is there not still a weeping over the exile, only not over the sins?
blocks.text: No: the Rebbe said there shouldn't be a weeping over the exile anymore. Now we're ready to have the joy that *Moshiach* is already coming: it's coming. That's what the Rebbe said: you don't have to do the weeping anymore, now we're doing the joy already. And the weeping over the sins of youth is also not necessary: you can just leave the sins of youth. And by the way, this is one of the reasons not to go against the *shluchim* (the Rebbe's emissaries), because they're preparing everybody for us.

This is the first level. These people have to put on *tefillin* and start keeping *Shabbos*. That's what he is saying: leaving the sins of youth is the preparation for these three levels of weeping. First the weeping of *bina*, that he doesn't understand the basic explanations in the first place, because it's hard to go through; then the second weeping, of *chachma*, when he realizes how far away the *Aibershter* is; and then the third weeping, of *bina*, when he understands that the thing is totally incomprehensible. But the preparation for that is the weeping in *tikkun chatzos* over the sins of youth, which gets him to leave the sins of youth.

And right now it's very important to remember these *shluchim*. There are *shluchim* all over the place, getting people to do the first step of *teshuva*. In regard to the external world, they're basically saving it: they're bringing about this first level, the *teshuva tata'a*, which basically means getting people to start putting on *tefillin*, and keeping *Shabbos*, and eating kosher, and learning *mishnayos*, doing *ChiTaS*, and all this kind of business.

blocks.text: "Did I tell you about the guy from Singapore?" It's the *shluchim* convention this weekend in New York. Rabbi Markel's son Mendel met an old friend of his from yeshiva who is now the *shliach* of Singapore, and this guy asked him, "Is your father here?" He thought Rabbi Markel might have come for the *shluchim* convention, as some people do. "No, he's not. What do you need him for?" So these guys, they're the guys who supply, for instance, you guys: the first time a *shliach* went out there and started the place, and now there's kosher food there and a synagogue for you. So it's very important.

sections.title: The sign of the true thing: the lower return, our days, and the tevuna of the Essence
sections.summary: Without the preparation a man fools himself: weeping alone, joy alone, or neither deep, and it does not last. A *Chassidus* that does not make a man more observant is not *Chassidus*; in our days the Rebbe says to go over the top, without weeping. And what is learned here is the *tevuna* of the Essence itself, given down to the lowest.

phrases.he: ואם לא, יטעה את עצמו באחד מאלה,
phrases.en: And if not, he will fool himself in one of these:

phrases.en: either weeping alone

blocks.text: **And if not, he will fool himself**: if he is studying *Chassidus* and he is not putting on *tefillin*, he is fooling himself.

And by the way, that's the whole reason why Rabbi Markel is getting so involved with pointing out the *mitzvos* of the children of Noah. By them too there is a matter of studying, because they have two *mitzvos* that have to do with the *Aibershter*. But by them too, if they don't want to keep the seven *mitzvos*, they are making a mistake: "he will fool himself".

**either weeping alone**: some people only like to cry, but they're not happy about it. **or joy alone**: they're just happy, and there's no weeping at all. Or else **they are not in their truth and their depth**: they are not really true and deep.

If the *Shechina* is *mamash* inside of you, how come people can go and be whatever they are? Because it's as if the *Shechina* is in exile, and shines on him from a very faraway place.

**all those who keep falling from their level**: one minute they flipped out with happiness or with crying, and then it's gone. **and with a few hindrances and opponents**, with a little bit of a hindrance, somebody going against it, **the ropes of connection are torn from his heart completely**, and he's not tied to it anymore. They don't want the food of *chachma*.

phrases.en: Therefore, whoever truly desires closeness to G-d

blocks.text: Somebody who really wants to be close to the *Aibershter* **should always make a great preparation in his soul, in *tikkun chatzos***. And he shouldn't fool himself, to *mamash* lose his soul for nothing.

And as we said, in our days it's not anymore a matter of *tikkun chatzos*, but there is a matter of doing *teshuva*. So what's the sign? The sign is this: if you don't see a *teshuva tata'a*, there's no real *teshuva ila'a* either. There's no such thing that a person should study *Chassidus* and not become *frummer* (more observant). And not only that: if it doesn't make you *frummer*, then it's not *Chassidus* that you're learning. ("It's a totally different *Chassidus*.") No, it might be *Chassidus*, but you didn't learn it properly. The Frierdiker Rebbe says that if it doesn't make you *frummer*, it's not *Chassidus*: it's *Chassidus* from the *ba'al davar*, the adversary, because it looks more sophisticated.

In other words, *tikkun chatzos* is the weeping over the sins of youth, he says. So the way we apply it now is like this. *Tikkun chatzos* is the most external level of *teshuva*. And now the Rebbe said that *teshuva* and everything is not done in a way of weeping anymore. That was only until the days of the Frierdiker Rebbe, whose motto was *l'alter l'teshuva, l'alter l'geula*, immediately to *teshuva*, immediately to the redemption. And the Rebbe says that in our days it is *l'alter l'geula*.

blocks.question: But wait a minute: doesn't that totally disagree with what he says here, that there is no joy without weeping?
blocks.text: No, because he just told you that the weeping was in the exile. We did the weeping; we already did the weeping, and now we're ready for happiness. And it's not that the weeping is not there. In the exile the happiness was also there, except that the weeping was open and the joy was hidden. Now it's the other way around: the joy is open and the weeping is hidden. But *tikkun chatzos* is the thing that fixes up the sins of youth, the basic level of *teshuva*; and if you don't see this basic level of *teshuva* in a person, he's not really studying *Chassidus*.

blocks.title: The letter from Toronto
blocks.text: He got a letter from a guy in Toronto, a *Lubavitcher bochur* (young man), apparently. His father is getting mixed up with these people called Bnei Baruch, a close sister group of the Berg people; they're also Ashlagians. He looked through their stuff: they're total heretics. And the boy is wondering what's happening, because it looks like his father is becoming more and more lax with the *mitzvos*.

blocks.text: So that's the sign. He's telling you here: that's the sign. If he's becoming lax with the *mitzvos*, it's not real *Kabbala* or *Chassidus*. Because you can't say, "Oh, but I'm doing *Kabbala*, I'm doing *teshuva ila'a*." It says that if you're doing *teshuva ila'a*, the *teshuva tata'a* is automatically included, and there should be an automatic improvement in your level of doing the *mitzvos*.

blocks.text: **(With all this the main reason will also be understood for the great rule said in the name of the Maggid, of blessed memory**... They stop at a word their copy has unclearly, and the tape is turned over.

He thinks it's a mistake, a typo; it might be *tivi'im*. ("What does *tivi'im* mean? The natural scientists or something like that?" "I don't know. We got stuck on this word also.") From what follows, "that it is a vessel of preparation for the true thing, in self-sacrifice in One", the **natural *mara shchora* (melancholy)** must be the simple crying he spoke of before: the natural weeping. (Is there a footnote there, on the sins of youth? There is not.) **that it is a vessel of preparation for the true delight, in self-sacrifice in "One"**, and for the acceptance of the yoke, as is explained at length in the *Kuntres*.

The basic point, if you take the basic point of the end part, is just saying that *teshuva tata'a* is a necessary *kli*, a preparation, to get into learning the deeper *Chassidus*. According to the way of the Mitteler Rebbe, you couldn't really understand *Chassidus* properly unless you had a big preparation, with crying and stuff like that. Which the Rebbe says now is different. First of all, the Rebbe Maharash said *lechatchila ariber*, and the Rebbe said two: the Rebbe Maharash's *lechatchila ariber*, and his own *lechatchila ariber*, which is to start living like *Moshiach*. (Here, he brings a footnote on "as the Maggid said", in the *Maamarim Kuntreisim*; they will look it up after.)

So, to recap the chapter: it seems that at the end he is backing off from what he said at the beginning. He was saying that *bina* is the main thing, and later on it seems it switched over to the *avoda* of *Malchus*: he switched away from *teshuva ila'a* to *teshuva tata'a*. Except that, if you notice, he said, "Well, this is the preparation for what I said before. That's what I said before; but if you're not doing the *mitzvos*, then you're not doing nothing. It all goes together with being *frum*." And if you're not *frum*, you have to start doing that along with this; otherwise this whole thing is not going to work, basically. And what Shimon said about what the Rebbe said, that now it's *lechatchila ariber*: that's basically because now everybody is a *tinok shenishba* (a child taken captive), so they don't really have a sin of youth. That's why it can work.

blocks.title: "Hey, king-o baby, let's dance"
blocks.text: You can't be a rebel against the kingdom and at the same time do a *teshuva ila'a*, and say, "Hey, king-o baby, let's dance together." "What are you talking about? You're a rebel against the kingdom, I'm going to hang you. You can't dance together with me. You're a rebel. A rebel is a rebel: you cast off the yoke." So now the thing is that they are not rebels.

And there are various reasons the Rebbe gave. Also, because the weeping was already done: the whole exile was already done. He said that since what happened, and especially in the Second World War and things like that, the Jews already had such a weeping that it's already time for the joy. So that's the basic matter here. It's not that the Rebbe is disagreeing with this; he just adjusted it for our days.

And basically we know from our own experience that you can do *lechatchila ariber*, and go straight to *daas Havaya*, which is what the Rebbe means by starting to live like *Moshiach*: as it says, in the time of *Moshiach* the only thing everybody will do is *daas Havaya*. The footnote says, "And this I heard explained from my father, of blessed memory, who heard from the Maggid, of blessed memory, that a person cannot come to receive the true secrets of the Torah and the true deep comprehension of the *Ein Sof* unless there is fixed in his soul the natural and essential kingship of Heaven, rooted in him from his youth precisely." But that too is not like that anymore. He is talking about a person who is not really a *frum* person from his youth, who didn't *mamash* grow up like that: it's very hard for him to think of becoming a guy who is going to learn these things and actually be affected by them.

But the Rebbe said it's not like that by us anymore. So what he was saying is that the whole beginning of the chapter was on *bina*, and on the matter of *teshuva ila'a*; and at the end he said, but there's no such thing as *teshuva ila'a* without *teshuva tata'a* first. Okay: that was until the Rebbe Maharash. The Rebbe Maharash said *lechatchila ariber*, which means forget the *teshuva tata'a* and go straight to the *teshuva ila'a*. And the Rebbe said even farther than that: really forget even the *teshuva ila'a*; we're going to *pnimiyus bina*, the inner core of *bina*. Not even just *bina*, but the inner core of *bina*, into the actual Essence. And that's chapter 6.

It's a very fantastic chapter. The main thing of chapter 6 is that the *bina*, which is basically the study of this book, the study of the explanations, precisely because it does not grab onto the Essence of G-dliness at all (since if you understand it, it must not be the Essence; right now we're understanding stuff, so it must mean we're understanding certain explanations, because all *bina* can do is understand explanations, and if you understand an explanation, it's not the Essence), awakens what it says: "*bina* is the heart", with the eye of the intellect which is in the heart everything is seen. And the heart sees precisely with *bina*.

And this is the basic thing of *bina*: *bina* is the perfect vacuum cleaner. Not only is it a perfect vacuum cleaner in that it gives a perfect vacuum; the more you put into it, the bigger the vacuum gets. The more he understands, the more he understands that there's nothing there: that the whole thing is just an explanation. But precisely because of that there is the *kushya*, the difficulty, of *bina*: the whole matter of *bina* is that he really wants to understand the thing itself, not just the explanation. That's the real thing of *bina*.

And you can actually see this by looking at your own *bina*. When you want to understand something, you want to understand the actual thing, not just the explanation. And therefore, since he realizes he's just understanding the explanation, the first difficulty is that he doesn't understand the explanation yet. Then, when he understands the explanation, this immediately brings about the flash of *chachma*, and with the flash of *chachma* he can see the *hafla'a*, the thing he didn't understand; and not only that, he can see how far away from understanding it is. And this brings about the second *kli* of *bina*, which is the third *kli*: not that he didn't understand the explanation, because he understands the explanation fine, perfectly, but that he cannot understand the Essence. And then what happens? It's not that he can understand the Essence; but the Essence can make itself understood. The *Aibershter* is all-powerful.

And that's why it says *mosrin*, "given over". He doesn't get it himself: it's given to him. And this is the whole matter of Torah, by the way. It says, "Moshe received the Torah from Sinai and gave it over to Yehoshua." It's not that Moshe got it *mamash* through his own effort. Through his own effort he reached the level to be able to receive the Torah; but the Torah itself is totally beyond Moshe. It's called the Torah of Moshe, but really it comes from the *Aibershter*, and the Torah of the *Aibershter* included everything: there's the written Torah and the oral Torah. On the oral Torah too it says, "and G-d said to Moshe": it was also given to Moshe. And it will be opened up by *Moshiach*. This is it: this is the opening up by *Moshiach*, and that is into the Essence.

"If it's so simple, the explanation is right here in front of us: it's not just given, it was already given, here it is, and anybody can grab it." No, he can't. They can't. People who don't even have the preparation, because they don't put on *tefillin* every day, and they eat pig, so their whole brain is made out of pig meat.
