blocks.text: So the basic thing is like this: precisely because of this, and that's the thing of *bina*, *bina* connects all the way up. All the *binos* connect together, more than other things. Other things, when they come down, are really not the original thing anymore. When *chachma* comes down from the *chachma* of the *Ein Sof* to *chachma* of *Atzilus*, to *chachma* of *Beriya*, all the way to the *chachma* of this world, it's not *mamash* the same *chachma* anymore, even though it's all the *chachma* of the *Aibershter*, even the *chachma* of putting the world together. And certainly *chesed*: as Avraham Avinu said, the love on his level was not like the love from upstairs. But with explanation, what we are learning here is the explanation of the *Aibershter* Himself. "Yes, but it came down many levels." He says: "Yes; precisely that shows that it is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof* Himself."

This is not just a lower *tevuna* of *Asiya*. Just the opposite: the fact that it came down to such a level that even we can understand it shows that this is a *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*, who came up with this explanation. As we learned before, precisely the *ish tevuna* can bring the *tevuna* to the sheep, the water to the sheep. So this is not a *tevuna* that came through *hishtalshelus*: the other things come through *hishtalshelus*, and this is coming direct. "But there's a *hislabshus*, an enclothing, into *meshalim*, and the *meshalim* into *meshalim*, and the *meshalim* into *meshalim*." He says, yes, but in the *tevuna* itself there is no enclothing. It's *mamash* the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter*.

Because that's the whole matter of *tevuna*: to enclothe it in *meshalim* until a little baby can understand. And that's like what it says about the Ark and the Holy of Holies: in the first Temple the *Shechina* was in the Ark, and it was like *Malchus* of *Atzilus* enclothed only in *Malchus* of *Beriya*. The *Shechina* was actually there, and there was no further enclothing into *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. That's what he says in the *Tanya*, basically the last chapter of the *Tanya*.

But this book here is actually higher than the Holy Ark. It is the actual *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*. You say, but it does go through the various levels of enclothing. He says no: that's the whole matter of *tevuna*. The *Ein Sof* wanted to have this *tevuna*: "His understanding is beyond searching", "His understanding is beyond number". His *tevuna*, totally beyond any searching, can take and explain something that's beyond searching, like a *tzimtzum*; and He wanted to explain it to us. And this whole enclothing is not really an enclothing: even though it's an enclothing in *meshalim*, that's *mamash* the matter of the *tevuna* itself. So this is not a *tevuna* of *Asiya*. This is the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter*, literally. What we're learning here, the explanation itself, is literally the Essence.

And you say, how's that possible? If you can understand it, it means it's not the Essence. Over here, he says, you've got to go that extra step: "The simple one believes everything." We believe that this is what it is. The *Aibershter* wanted, and that's what this book really tells us, the whole matter of what a *tzimtzum* was and everything: the *Aibershter* wanted to explain it to us, and that's what He did. And this is the explanation of the *Aibershter* Himself, the Torah of the *Aibershter*, *pnimiyus haTorah*, the inner Torah. This is what the *Aibershter* explained to us, and it's not even from *Malchus* of *Atzilus*: it is literally from the *Ein Sof* Himself. It's *mamash* the *Ein Sof* standing here and explaining it to us, and the explanation itself is the *Aibershter*, literally.

As it says, "the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Torah and Israel are all one". And this is *mamash* the inner Torah, the *shaashua hamelech b'atzmuso*, the King's delight in Himself. It says that David called it "delights" and that's why he was punished; but that was because he was speaking of the delights in the outside. This is the King's delight in Himself. In other words, this is not really the explanation of the world. This is G-d's explanation of Himself: *mamash* the actual King's delight in Himself. This is it.

And that's why we're absolutely invincible. Because we're not going with even the light of *Atzilus*, or the lights of *Tohu* and vessels of *Tikkun*; we're not going with even lights. We're going past that: with the *Maor* (the source of light) itself, literally. *Chassidus*. And when you say, where are you getting such a crazy thing? Look all over *Chassidus*: it says *Chassidus* is the *Maor*. In other words, the *Chassidus* itself is the *Aibershter*. And it says in *Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus* that *Moshiach* and *Chassidus* and the *Aibershter* and the Rebbe are all one thing.

Chapter 6, before we get to chapter seven. There are two main matters in chapter six. One is the general matter of joy and weeping, which really applies in all the *sefiros* and in any kind of *avoda*. And basically the matter of weeping and joy is the matter of the *Keser*. The *Keser* of a *sefira* means that according to how bad you feel for not having it, that's how good you feel for having it: that is its *taanug*.

blocks.text: And according to the *taanug* will be the *ratzon*: if you feel real bad, that means you want it real bad. That is one more thing that will also apply in later chapters, when we get into the *Kesarim* (the crowns): a *ratzon* and a *taanug* are the same thing, but the *ratzon* really comes from the opposite of the *taanug*. The more you don't have the *taanug*, the more you have a *ratzon*: the *ratzon* comes precisely from the weeping part. When you're actually getting what you want, you're satiated. The *ratzon* is from the lack; the lack of the *taanug* makes the *ratzon* get stronger. That's in general, and that's the whole thing he was saying: precisely when he feels the lack, that will make him study harder, for instance.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: The Olympics and the spitting contest
blocks.text: And the same is really in any *midda*, like the guys who go for the Olympics. Why do they try so hard? Because they feel a lack, which other people don't: "I don't feel that lack, I could care less." And why do they feel the lack? Because if they would win, they would feel the great enjoyment. As far as he's concerned, if he would win the spitting contest, for instance, or something like that, what does he care? It's not a big enjoyment there. So you see that weeping and joy are really like that in all the *sefiros*, not just in *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: But he explains that in the matter of *Chassidus* in particular, in terms of the weeping and the joy, the *bina* is the strongest of all of them. Why? Because there is absolutely no satiation, no *taanug*; just the opposite. The more you understand, the more you start understanding that it's not only hard to understand, it's past understanding totally, beyond understanding. So the lack of *taanug* becomes more and more pronounced the more you get it. The more you understand, the more you want. And in *bina* it's infinite, because the lack is 100%: as he said, if you understand it, it's not the Essence. In all the other things, like the *hafla'a*, the *hafla'a* you are getting is from the Essence: the *hafla'a* of the Essence is what you're getting the insight into.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So if you have the *hafla'a*, it is precisely the Essence. And even what he talked about at the end of the chapter, the accepting of the yoke of the kingship of Heaven: it too is precisely of the Essence. So there is a certain amount that it does get; whereas by *bina* it's totally, totally gone.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: But *bina* always has two sides, as we learned going back to chapter two: in *bina* there are two things, *bina* and *tevuna*. The general matter of *bina* and *tevuna* is also, in *bina* itself (and if you look in the whole chapter there, it talks about it a lot), from up to down and from down to up. From down to up is the receiver, the student; from up to down is the teacher. In general those two are really *bina* and *tevuna*. *Bina* is from down to up, because *bina* means to understand the actual thing: you're going up, to understand the thing. That's what *hisbonenus* is. *Hisbonenus* means learning: the real thing of *hisbonenus* is the student, going up.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Even though, as he explains in that whole chapter, there is also a *hisbonenus* by the teacher, who has to contemplate how to teach the thing, that is really not the *hisbonenus* of *bina*. That's the *hisbonenus* of *tevuna*: really *tevuna sheb'tevuna*, not *bina sheb'bina*. To think how to teach the other guy is not really *bina sheb'bina*, because you're not trying to understand it. To have *tevuna* you already have to understand it, and now he contemplates it to get a good *kelita*, a good taking hold of it; and that is really *tevuna sheb'tevuna*. In general, *bina* goes up from the student to the teacher, and *tevuna*, that was the whole definition of *tevuna*: the *ish tevuna* can teach it to others. "Deep waters, the man of understanding draws them out."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So the same as by the *bina*: of all the ways of going up, *bina*, meaning *hisbonenus*, *bina sheb'bina*, is the strongest, because it is *mamash* directed at the Essence itself. In the other ones there is not a total lack of the Essence, so there is not a total desire for the Essence. But he really didn't talk about the other side of it, the *tevuna* part. In terms of the flow from the *Aibershter* down, it is precisely *tevuna* that comes down with no enclothing whatsoever. That is the matter of "deep waters, the man of understanding draws them out".
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: Shlomo's three thousand meshalim
blocks.text: To be an *ish tevuna*, to be able to explain it to somebody else, as it explains in various other places, he has to understand it even better. The *tevuna* has to go into the depth of *chachma*, into the inner core of *Abba*, the inner core of *Atik*. This is what he explains later on about what a big *chacham* (wise man) is. It says a big *chacham* was Shlomo. What shows what a big *chacham* he was? That he could make three thousand *meshalim*. Which, if you think about it, wait a minute: three thousand *meshalim* is not a matter of *chachma* at all. It's a matter of *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: Shlomo's three thousand meshalim
blocks.text: The whole matter of a *mashal* is to enclothe the thing, not just to bring it down, but to enclothe it in a *davar zar*, something foreign: to bring it into something else, outside of itself. That's the whole matter of a *mashal*: a *mashal* means *tevuna*. And yet precisely the *tevuna* proved how smart he was. That's also what it says: Moshe Rabbeinu found wise men, but men of understanding he couldn't find. That means that *tevuna* is really harder to find than *bina*. It's higher.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Now what do the three thousand *meshalim* mean? That he was able to enclothe the *chachma* level after level, one more, down to three thousand levels. So Shlomo HaMelech is now saying that the *Aibershter* Himself enclothed everything farther and farther down; as a matter of fact, the whole *seder hishtalshelus*. It says in *Pasach Eliyahu*: why did He create the world? To show people. It's a *mashal*, to explain the *Aibershter* to people. This is a teaching process: as we said, the whole *tzimtzum* is like a teacher. Why did He make the *tzimtzum*?
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So look at all the other ones. When the *chachma* comes down in three thousand *meshalim*, the *chachma* that is coming into the end of the last *mashal* is not the same *chachma* as in the first *mashal*, even though in a way it's a bigger *chachma* to enclothe it in a *mashal*. The actual thing that comes out in the last *mashal* is just a very big *tzimtzum* of *chachma*. And it's like this in all the *sefiros*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Even though, to enclothe it, it takes a very big power, so in a way you have to say that the power of the *tzimtzum* is at least as great as the power of the *Ein Sof*. As a matter of fact, you really have to say that the power of the *tzimtzum* is greater than the power of the *Ein Sof*, because it's the power of the *tzimtzum* that allows the *Ein Sof* in the first place, when you're not limited to something. To the point that you have to say it's *mamash* the same power, or maybe even a greater power: a power of the Essence. But the power of the *Ein Sof* is also a power of the Essence.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: A voice that breaks a few trees
blocks.text: Even so, in all the *sefiros*, take for instance the thing of power: "the voice of G-d breaks the cedars", breaks down the trees. You say, that's a very big *tzimtzum*. Really, it's almost a joke. What do you mean, it breaks down the trees? What's the big deal? The voice of the *Aibershter* can do a lot more than just break down a few trees. So what's the story? He says, "Yes, but if He would show you a voice that would break more than a few trees, you wouldn't be able to receive it." It would blow everything up.

blocks.title: A voice that breaks a few trees
blocks.text: So what does He do? He just breaks a few trees, and you're scared; and He makes a few lightning flashes, and everybody is scared and says, "Wow!" And then they all start praying, like by Yona: the waves were going up and down, everybody got scared, they started praying. But really the power of the *Aibershter* is much greater. That's for sure.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So that's in all the *sefiros* except for *tevuna*. Because in *tevuna*, the whole matter of *tevuna* is that he enclothes it in a way that goes down to the sheep. The main thing of *tevuna* is not the depth of the *chachma*. It's that he took the depth of the *chachma* and brought it all the way out to the lowest level. But it's the same depth, the same depth: the depth of the *chachma*. The *bina*, when you do the *hisbonenus*, catches the inner core of *Ima*, the inner core of *Abba*, and gets to understand it; and then, through the vessel of *tevuna*, he can take that depth of *Abba* and bring it out to the sheep.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: And that's the matter of *tevuna*. The matter of *tevuna* is not the depth of *chachma*: it's the shallowness of the sheep. That's the real matter of *tevuna*, the *tevuna* itself, because that's the whole definition of *tevuna*. If he is very deep, no matter how deep he understands it, he's just a *tafsan*, because he understands it deep. The thing that makes him an *ish tevuna* is that he brought it out to the outermost, lowest level. And the lower the level, the bigger the *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So it means that, the same as the *bina* from down to up is the biggest one, and it is *mamash* grasping the Essence, the *tevuna* is also like that. Whereas all the other things, like the greatness of the *Aibershter*, the glory and splendor: you can't have the actual glory and splendor of the *Aibershter*. It'll blow you away. Not just blow us away: it will blow the whole universe away; and not only our universe, it will blow all of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* away, with *Adam Kadmon* and everything. And the same with everything, *netzach*, *hod*, all the other things: it will blow them away. Except for *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: The *tevuna*, the thing we're learning right now, *mamash* this book here: this is the *tevuna* of the Essence. Not the *tevuna* of the Essence enclothed in something. The *chachma* is enclothed in something here: the depth of the *chachma* is enclothed in *mashal* after *mashal* after *mashal*. You say, "Yes, well, it's really the *chachma* of the *Aibershter*, but it's all in enclothing." Yes: the *chachma* is in enclothing, and the *chesed*. Right now we feel that the *Aibershter* is doing us a *chesed*. But if we would really feel the *chesed*, we would go crazy: we would start crying and laughing and rolling on the floor. And it would be even more than that; and that's feeling just a little bit of the *chesed*. If you'd feel all the *chesed*, you'd stop existing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: But the *tevuna* is precisely the opposite. That it's a tiny little drop for a little, tiny sheep: that's the whole matter of *tevuna*. And that it's precisely to lowlifes like us: that's the whole matter of *tevuna*, to teach it to the sheep. Not to teach it to the big shots. And not only that: the lower the sheep, the bigger the *tevuna*. That's *mamash* the matter of the *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So all the other *sefiros* are coming down with a *tzimtzum*: the *chesed*, the *gevura* (we get the fantastic *gevura* of the *Aibershter* here), the *tiferes*, that we see the fantastic glory of the *Aibershter* and things like that, the glory and splendor; and also the *Malchus* that's coming down to us through this is still coming down with *tzimtzumim*. But the *tevuna*: this is the original *tevuna*. This is the *tevuna*, not a *tzimtzum* of the *tevuna*; just the opposite. On the last *mashal*, on the 3,000th *mashal*, is the biggest *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: That's the original *tevuna*. As a matter of fact, that's what proves that he's an *ish tevuna*: the whole thing that proves he's an *ish tevuna* is precisely the last *mashal*, where it comes to the sheep. If he can't get it to the sheep, even if he understands it all the way down, he's not an *ish tevuna*. He's just a *chacham* or a *mevin*: he didn't bring it to them. So this thing here is literally the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter* Himself. It's the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*, the *tevuna* of the Essence, *mamash* literally.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: And that's the other thing: when we grasp it, even though we're grasping an explanation, you say, "But you're just grasping an explanation. There's no comprehension of the *mahus*; there's only comprehension of an explanation." It says, yes, but the explanation itself is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*, and we are grasping the actual explanation. And you say, "Yes, but that's not how He understands." No: that's not the *bina* of the *Ein Sof*; this is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*. This is to explain. This is Torah: the actual explanation that the *Aibershter* gave us, the explanation He came up with; and we grasp it. When you grasp this explanation, you're *mamash* grasping the Essence. It's not like other things.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: An explanation of a hurricane
blocks.text: When you're grasping an explanation of an airplane, it's not the same as grasping an airplane. When you grasp an explanation of a hurricane, it's not *mamash* like an actual hurricane. But here it's a different thing. Why? Because there, when you grasp an explanation of how a hurricane works, what you're grasping is the *tevuna* of the explainer. And here, that's exactly it: you're grasping the *tevuna* of the explainer, literally. And "His understanding is beyond searching": that's what you're grasping.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: And not only that: as we learned before, upstairs there is no such thing as *tevuna*; there is the Essence. The *tevuna* is the Essence; especially since we're not even talking here about the *tevuna* of *Yachid*: this is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*. And this is the whole thing, as it explains: the whole *tzimtzum* was a descent of the SaG, *Malchus* of *tevuna*, and the letters, the separate, external explanations, come out from *Malchus* of *tevuna*. So we're literally catching the *Malchus* of *tevuna* of the *Aibershter*. And you're *mamash* grasping it: right now it's going into our heads, to the point that we can actually think about it. That means that literally the *Aibershter* is going into our heads. The *Chassidus* is literally the *Aibershter* actually going into us: "and I will dwell among them".

blocks.text: And this is a bigger thing than even the Holy Ark. The *Shechina* in the Holy Ark was *Malchus* of *Atzilus* enclothed in *Malchus* of *Beriya*. This is *Malchus* of *tevuna* of the Essence, totally not enclothed at all; the Essence, which is higher than *Yachid*. Over there, even in *Yachid*, there is no real separate thing: "not of any of these attributes at all". And it's not enclothing at all. It's the actual intellect of the giver going into the receiver.

blocks.text: So that's the whole thing of *bina*, why the whole thing is precisely *bina*: those are the two things. First of all, from down to up, it's the perfect vacuum cleaner. And secondly, from up to down, it's the perfect opposite of a vacuum: the actual thing itself. Like the vacuum cleaner, where the zero is a total zero, not almost zero like by the other things, *kula kamei k'la chashiv*: it's *ein od milvado*. So from down to up it's *ayin*, a total *ayin*: the *bina* from down to up is a total nothing. And from up to down, the *tevuna* is *mamash* *ein od milvado*: it's the actual Him.

blocks.text: And this is also the matter of *teshuva ila'a*. In *teshuva ila'a* it says, "and the soul returns to G-d": not almost, all the way. So that's a very big thing about *bina*, a very big thing about *hisbonenus*, a very big thing about *Chassidus* in general, and especially about this particular book in particular: that it's literally the *Aibershter* Himself, bigger than the Holy Ark.

blocks.text: ("Wow.") Yes, that's exactly what it is. But again, the wow is a thing of *chachma*: that's *hafla'a*. Wow means *hafla'a*. And you're not getting the full wow, because if you would get the full wow, you'd explode. ("I'm getting the wow according to the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter*.") Yes, but the *chachma* is enclothed: it's a *tzimtzum* of a wow. But the *tevuna* itself is *mamash* the *Aibershter*: the *tevuna* itself is *mamash* the *tevuna* of the Essence.

blocks.text: And that's also what Reb Hillel Paritcher explains. He actually uses a *mashal* for the whole beginning of the chain of *yesh* from *ayin*: it is *tevuna*. It's a *yesh*. The whole matter of the *yesh* is precisely in *tevuna*, more than in *bina*: *bina* is called a *yesh*, but that is really in relation to *chachma*, while *tevuna* is the actual *yesh* of the receiver, which doesn't change the whole way down. Reb Hillel Paritcher explains it with a teacher and a student: when the teacher gives the student an explanation, in the giving of the explanation, through the *tzimtzumim* according to the receiver, he actually gives himself.

blocks.text: Because the *tevuna* is the actual *tevuna*. It's not a *tzimtzum* of the *tevuna*; just the opposite. And that's the *tevuna*. ("I never *chapped* that that's the *tevuna*.") The more it goes down, the more the Essence is the *tevuna*. All the other things, the more they go down, the less of the Essence they are. But by the *tevuna* it's the opposite way around: the more it goes down, the more *tevuna* there is, the more it is the *tevuna* of the *ish tevuna*.

blocks.text: And also, when you grasp part of the *etzem*, you grasp the whole *etzem*. And not only that: what we're talking about is the *tevuna* of the Essence. Not even like by *Yachid*, where it's non-separate: by the Essence it's *mamash* the Essence, and there's no such thing as a part of the Essence. So it's *mamash* a grasp of the actual *etzem*. In other words, when you're learning *Chassidus*, when you're learning this thing, even though you're grasping an explanation, it makes no difference: this explanation itself is the *etzem*. It's the *etzem* of the *tevuna*. And that is the whole matter of the chain of *yesh* from *ayin*, and it is precisely by *Chassidus*, more than by any other part of Torah, which is really only an enclothing.

blocks.text: Because there the whole thing is enclothing: what's being explained there is not the Essence. As it says in the *Tanya*, the *mitzva* and the reason of the *mitzva* are the will and the *chachma* of the *Aibershter*: the *Aibershter* wanted that if such and such a guy would do like this, and such and such a guy would do like that, the ruling should come out like that. That's what it says in the *Tanya*. But it still comes in an enclothing in a *davar zar*, something foreign. So it's not really the whole *chachma*.

blocks.title: Passing the salt
blocks.text: For instance, you're sitting at the table, and your father is sitting three people away from you, and he asks for the salt. So you have a *chachma*: you pass the salt to the guy sitting next to you, and he passes it to the next guy sitting next to him, and he passes it to him. That's *chachma*. But it's a big enclothing of *chachma* in a total *davar zar*, even though it's *mamash* your own *chachma*: it's a big *tzimtzum* of it. It's not *mamash* that through this you get the whole actual *chachma*, even though in a way you do. So when you learn the Talmud, you're *mamash* *chapping* the actual *chachma*, but it's still through a big *tzimtzum*, an enclothing in a *davar zar*: if the donkey knocks over something, then this guy says that his donkey knocked over something, etc.

blocks.text: But over here it's a whole different thing. First of all, the *tevuna* is the actual *tevuna* itself, not a *tzimtzum* of the *tevuna*; just the opposite: the more it goes down, the more it is the *tevuna*. And secondly, this is the *tevuna* of the thing itself, of *shaashuei hamelech b'atzmuso*, the King's delight in Himself.

reviewQuestions.question: Why must weeping and joy come together from one contemplation, and what is the sign that nothing went into the soul?
How does comprehension by negation (*hasagas hashlila*) differ from the sight of *chachma*, and what does the mountain that keeps getting bigger show?
Why does the power of *bina* come from not understanding, and why does that make the Essence its real object?
What are the three levels of weeping, and how does each awaken the next?
If comprehension is only of a *tzimtzum* of the light, how can the joy of *bina* be in the Essence?
What is the sign that a man's *Chassidus* is real, and how does the Rebbe's *lechatchila ariber* fit with the chapter's call to weep in *tikkun chatzos*?
